Scheme: Mukhyamantri Uchcha Shiksha Shodh Protsahan Yojana
Section: Documents Required
- All required documents must be submitted in accordance with the guidelines specified for the research proposal by the concerned institution.

Scheme: Mukhyamantri Uchcha Shiksha Shodh Protsahan Yojana
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
- Researchers must submit their research proposals online through the Samarth portal ([https://uttarakhand.samarth.ac.in/index/site/login](https://uttarakhand.samarth.ac.in/index.php/site/login)). - During the application process, the proposal must be uploaded and forwarded by the institution’s Principal or Registrar within fifteen days of submission; otherwise, it will automatically move to the next level. 
 - The proposal will then be evaluated by the Evaluation Committee, and the research grant will be released in three installments via DBT to the institution’s Research and Development Cell account.

- Upon the written request of the Principal Investigator, the Principal or Registrar must make the grant available to the Principal Investigator or Researcher within three days. If this is not done, the State Research and Development Cell Committee must be informed through the Director of Education with clear written reasons, and the final decision will rest with the Secretary, Higher Education/Committee.
 - The first installment, amounting to 50% of the grant, will be released upon approval of the research proposal. 
 - The second installment, amounting to 30%, will be released only after submission of the utilization certificate. 
 - The third and final installment, amounting to 20%, will be released upon completion of the research work.

- The research must be original and in accordance with UGC standards. 
 - A Research Assistant will receive a stipend of ₹5,000 per month from the release of the first installment until the completion of the research work.

> **Login to apply for the scheme:**

**Step 02:** Enter Password & Captcha and click on ‘Login’.
**Step 03:** After successful login, click on ‘Apply for Services’ and then ‘View all Available Services’
**Step 04:** Now, you can search for the scheme and click on the scheme to go ahead and fill out the application form.
**Step 05:** Enter your Parivar Pehchan Patra number - Family ID and click on “Click here to Fetch Family Data”, which displays the family members registered under the given Family ID.

**Step 06:** Select the beneficiary/applicant name and enter the OTP that is being sent to the selected family member for verification. Click on “Click to Verify”

Scheme: "Interest Subvention on Working Capital" under the "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme"
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
**Registration Process**
**Step 1:** Visit the [dedicated portal](https://atisis.assam.gov.in/atsisver/login.html) of "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives" Scheme. Click on the "New User Registration" option.
**Step 2:** In the registration form, fill in basic details including name, mobile number, and email address. Create a username and password following the portal's password policy. Verify your mobile number through one-time password verification. Complete Captcha Code verification. Submit the registration form.

**Step 3:** Check your registered email for the account activation link. Click on the activation link to activate the account. Log in to the portal using registered credentials.
**Step 4:** Upload all supporting documents of eligibility in the prescribed format. Fill in complete unit details, including location, type of tea production, and capacity. Submit the unit registration form. Wait for registration approval.

**Application Process**
**Step 1:** Log in to the portal using registered credentials. Navigate to the "Apply for Benefits" section. Select the scheme component that you intend to apply for.
**Step 2:** Fill in the prescribed application form with all mandatory fields. Upload all supporting documents as mentioned in the portal. Ensure file formats and file size restrictions are followed as per the portal guidelines. Review all entered information for accuracy.
**Step 3:** Upload documents in the specified format and size. Ensure all documents are clear and legible. Complete document verification checklist.
**Step 4:** Review the complete application before submission. Apply online.
_*Note down the application reference number. Save a copy of the submitted application form._

_*Note down the application reference number. Save a copy of the submitted application form._
_*Applicants are strongly encouraged to save a copy of the submitted application, confirmation message, and application reference number for future reference and tracking purposes._

**Verification Process**
**Step 1:** Application is automatically routed to the concerned bank Bank verifies the amount of interest at 3%, borrower credentials, loan account classification as Standard, and interest servicing status. The Bank approves the application on the portal.
**Step 2:** After verification, if claims are found in order, the Commissioner, Industries & Commerce Department forwards claims to the Finance Department. The Finance Department processes the claim for online reimbursement through Direct Benefit Transfer.

**Disbursement Process**
The Finance Department releases the subsidy amount directly to the beneficiary's bank account. Short Message Service alerts sent for funds disbursement. The beneficiary receives the Direct Benefit Transfer in a registered bank account.
**Application Status Tracking**
Log in to the portal to check application status. Track application progress through different stages of verification. Receive Short Message Service alerts throughout the process, including registration, fund release, etc.
**Important Deadlines**
Claim on completion of every financial year.

Scheme: Small Business Scheme (Gujarat Gopalak Vikas Nigam)
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
**Step 1: Register on the Official Portal**

- Go to the [Official Website ](https://ggdconline.gujarat.gov.in/)of Gujarat Gopalak Development Corporation.- Scroll down on the homepage, find the "Small Business Scheme," and click on "Apply Now".
- You will be directed to the [application form](https://gbcdconline.gujarat.gov.in/SchemeSmallBusiness/AddEdit).
**Step 2: Access and Fill Out the Application Form**

- Select "Small Business Scheme", enter Unit Cost, and specify the Required Loan Amount.
- Provide Aadhaar, Ration, Voter ID, full name (Last, First, Father/Husband), address, district, taluka, village, PIN, date of birth, age (21-45 as of 14/08/2023), caste, subcaste, phone, mobile, email, gender, and marital status.
- Enter income certificate number, issue date, issuing officer's name, total annual family income (up to ₹ 3,00,000/-), and parent/guardian's occupation.

- Indicate if any family member works in a government or private job. If "Yes," provide their Name, Designation, Place, and Salary details.

- Select your Education Qualification: Uneducated, Educated, Graduation, Post Graduation, or Other Degree.
- If you have taken a past loan, select "Yes" or "No". If you selected "Yes", provide loan details (date, amount, paid, remaining) and your account number.
- Provide bank account number, bank name, branch name, name as per account, account type (Saving/Current), MICR code, and IFSC code.

**Step 3: Review and Final Submission**

- Carefully review each module. Use the preview option to examine the application before final submission. Fill out the provided "CAPTCHA" and Click on “Submit”.

**Track and Review Status**

- Applicant will receive an Application ID/Reference Number. Save or print the acknowledgement for future tracking.
- Go to the [Official Website](https://ggdconline.gujarat.gov.in/) of Gujarat Gopalak Development Corporation.- Scroll down and locate the Know App Status. Click on "Know App Status".
- Select the Scheme name, Enter App No., and Birth Date. Fill out the Captcha and click on Submit.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: What is the main objective of the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops"?
Answer: The main objective of the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops" is to encourage and support farmers in Gujarat to adopt high-density and ultra-high-density plantation techniques and to take up new cultivation of specific fruit crops by providing them with financial assistance for covering a portion of their cultivation costs.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: Who is responsible for implementing the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops"?
Answer: The scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops" is implemented by the Agriculture and Co-operation Department under the Government of Gujarat.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: Which fruit crops are eligible for financial assistance under the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops"?
Answer: The fruit crops eligible for financial assistance under the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops" include mango, guava, lemon, pomegranate, tissue culture banana, and papaya, which have been identified as suitable for cultivation under high-density, ultra-high-density, or new plantation methods.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: What is the amount of assistance provided for high-density and ultra-high-density plantation under the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops"?
Answer: Under the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops", the assistance for high-density and ultra-high-density plantations in crops such as mango, guava, lemon, and pomegranate ranges from ₹30,000/- to ₹40,000/- per hectare, subject to a maximum limit of 4 hectares per beneficiary farmer.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: How much financial assistance is provided for the cultivation of tissue culture banana under the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops"?
Answer: For the cultivation of tissue culture banana, the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops" provides financial assistance amounting to either 40% of the total expenditure incurred or ₹50,000/-, whichever is less, with an upper limit of 4 hectares per beneficiary farmer.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: What level of financial assistance is provided for papaya cultivation under the scheme?
Answer: The scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops" offers financial support for papaya cultivation, amounting to either 50% of the total cultivation cost or ₹30,000/- per hectare, whichever is less, enabling farmers to reduce their initial investment burden.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops"?
Answer: The scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops" is open to all farmers residing in Gujarat who are engaged in or intend to engage in the cultivation of the specified fruit crops on land that they own or cultivate, provided they meet the scheme’s conditions.

Scheme: Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit crops
Question: Is there any income limit for applying to the scheme "Assistance for Area Expansion in Fruit Crops"?

Answer: The scheme has a maximum area limit of 4 hectares per beneficiary farmer, and therefore no financial assistance will be provided for any area exceeding this limit under the scheme.

Scheme: DESW Internship Scheme

Answer: You will work on assigned topics related to welfare schemes, resettlement programs, healthcare policies, or administrative processes for veterans.

Answer: Yes, each intern must submit a comprehensive research report summarising observations, best practices, challenges, and recommendations.

Answer: Yes, based on satisfactory performance, the Department will issue a certificate of successful completion.

Answer: Yes, selected reports or excerpts may be published by the Department with due credit to the intern.

Scheme: DESW Internship Scheme

Scheme: DESW Internship Scheme

Answer: You must provide a resume, a statement of purpose (maximum 200 words), and an NOC from your parent institution if you are currently a student.

Scheme: DESW Internship Scheme

Answer: Yes, you can select the duration between 2 months to 1 year while applying, based on your availability.

Scheme: DESW Internship Scheme

Answer: Yes, internships are available year-round, depending on departmental requirements.

Question: What is the main objective of the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden" under the National Mission on Edible Oil – Oil Palm?
Answer: The main objective of the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden" is to significantly increase the production of oil palm in Gujarat while reducing the dependence on imports by providing financial assistance for the development of seed gardens and nurseries to eligible farmers.

Answer: The scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden" is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Gujarat, which is responsible for overseeing its execution and ensuring that the intended benefits reach the targeted farmers.

Scheme: National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm: Establishment of Seed Garden
Question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden"?
Answer: Any farmer residing in Gujarat who is engaged in or willing to engage in oil palm cultivation is eligible to apply for the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden" subject to fulfilling the specified requirements.

Scheme: National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm: Establishment of Seed Garden
Question: What type of financial assistance is provided for establishing a seed garden under the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden"?
Answer: Under the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden", a financial assistance of ₹80,00,000/- per seed garden is provided for creating the necessary infrastructure and for establishing a revolving fund to support its operational sustainability.

Question: What production capacity is required for a seed garden under the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden"?
Answer: A seed garden established under the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden" must have the capacity to produce 10,00,000 seedlings per year in order to be eligible for the provided assistance.

Scheme: National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm: Establishment of Seed Garden
Question: What is the minimum area requirement for a seed garden under the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden"?
Answer: The minimum area requirement for establishing a seed garden under the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden" is 15 hectares, which ensures adequate space for sustainable cultivation and production.

Scheme: National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm: Establishment of Seed Garden
Question: What financial assistance is available for nursery development under the scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden"?
Answer: The scheme "Establishment of Seed Garden" offers financial assistance of ₹40,00,000/- for the development of a nursery, covering the necessary infrastructure and initial operational support for oil palm cultivation.

- Copy of Aadhaar Card of the pregnant/lactating woman or child

Scheme: Integrated Child Development Services- Uttarakhand
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
Registration for availing benefits under the scheme is done either by the Anganwadi worker of the concerned area or by the beneficiary herself by visiting the nearest Anganwadi Centre. The Aadhaar card of the pregnant woman, lactating mother, or child is required for registration.
**The following benefits under the scheme are provided through Anganwadi workers, with beneficiary details registered on the Poshan Tracker mobile app:**

- **Cooked Food:** Pre-school children aged 3 to 6 years, registered at Anganwadi Centres, are provided breakfast and freshly cooked meals 25 days a month at the centres. - **Take Home Ration (THR):** Wheat and fortified rice are provided every month to children aged 6 months to 3 years, children aged 3 to 6 years, severely malnourished children, as well as pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadi workers. In addition, immunisation, vaccination, and health check-ups are provided with the support of the Health Department.

Answer: No, there is no income limit to avail benefits under this scheme.

Answer: Pre-school children aged 3 to 6 years receive breakfast and freshly cooked meals at Anganwadi Centres for 25 days each month.

Scheme: Integrated Child Development Services- Uttarakhand

Answer: Wheat and fortified rice are provided monthly to children aged 6 months to 6 years, severely malnourished children, and pregnant/lactating women.

Answer: Yes, all services provided under the scheme are completely free for eligible beneficiaries.

Scheme: Remembering Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears - Organisation of Special Dedicated Programmes
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should take a printout of the [prescribed format](https://www.goa.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Citizen-Charter-TAG.pdf) of the application form. Alternatively, the applicant may visit the office of Tiatr Academy of Goa to collect the form.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required). Sign the application form and mention the date.
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to -

**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to - 
***Tiatr Academy of Goa, AS-1 / AS-4, Block A, 2nd Floor, Campal Trade Centre, Opposite Kala Academy, Campal, Panaji, Goa, India – 403001***
_*Applicants are advised to save a copy of the submitted application form and any acknowledgment._
_*Applications are considered on a "First come First Serve" basis, subject to the availability of funds._
_*Tiatr Academy of Goa reserves the right to make any changes in the rules._
_*If adverse remarks are proved, Tiatr Academy of Goa reserves the right to disqualify the performance and refrain from making payment or recall the payment made._

##### **Post Application Processes**
**Step 1:****** ***Coordinate with Tiatr Academy of Goa***
The applicant must discuss and decide about the Chief Guest/Guest of Honour well in advance with Tiatr Academy of Goa, as the President or Vice President of Tiatr Academy of Goa will either be the Chief Guest/Guest of Honour at the function.
**Step 2:** ***Collect Banner and Materials***
The applicant must collect the banner from the office of Tiatr Academy of Goa before the performances (for tiatr) or arrange for backdrop with Tiatr Academy of Goa logo (for musical shows) and ensure proper display during all shows.
**Step 3:** ***Stage Performances***

**Step 3:** ***Stage Performances***
The applicant must stage the approved programme ensuring all conditions are met including free admission for public, proper acknowledgment of Tiatr Academy of Goa collaboration in all advertisements and media, and maintaining the specified duration for each type of performance.
**Step 4:** ***Documentation and Reporting***
The applicant must document the programme through photographs and submit 5 copies to Tiatr Academy of Goa for records, ensuring two photographs show the Tiatr Academy of Goa banner during performance.
**Step 5:** ***Submit Financial Documentation***

**Step 5:** ***Submit Financial Documentation***
The applicant must prepare and submit a detailed statement of expenditure with all original bills (stamped receipts if amount exceeds ₹5,000/-) to Tiatr Academy of Goa for reimbursement of approved expenses.
**Step 6:** ***Return Materials***
The applicant must return the Tiatr Academy of Goa banner to the office after all shows are completed to maintain the academy's inventory and complete the programme cycle.

##### ***Application Deadline***
Applications must reach the office of Tiatr Academy of Goa at least 30 days in advance along with typed script/lyrics.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What happens if I want to organize a cultural programme to honor a legendary performer from earlier generations who has passed away?
Answer: You can apply for this commemoration scheme which provides financial assistance, venue support, and publicity for celebrating jubilee or birth anniversaries of deceased Tiatr artistes. The programme must aim to educate younger generations about their contributions and sacrifices.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: Can both organizations and individual people apply for financial support to commemorate deceased cultural performers?
Answer: Yes, the scheme accepts applications from both organizing institutions and individuals who wish to celebrate jubilee or birth anniversaries of Tiatr artistes of yesteryears. The applicant can be either an institution or an individual person.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What type of approval do I need from the deceased artist's relatives before I can proceed with organizing a commemorative event?
Answer: You must obtain and submit a No Objection Certificate from the nearest family member or members of the deceased artiste. This certificate is mandatory and must be included with your application to the Tiatr Academy of Goa.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: How far in advance should I submit my application if I want to organize a memorial programme for a departed cultural figure?
Answer: Your complete application must reach the office of the Tiatr Academy of Goa at least 30 days before your proposed programme date. Applications are processed on a "First come First Serve" basis, subject to fund availability.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What documentation about my programme content and performers do I need to provide when applying for this cultural commemoration scheme?
Answer: You must submit a detailed proposal that includes the complete typed script, all lyrics to be presented during the programme, and the names of all artistes who will be performing. This comprehensive documentation is required at the application stage.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: Are there any restrictions on what I can say or present during the commemorative programme about government policies or religious matters?
Answer: Yes, you must ensure no adverse remarks are made in written or verbal form against any Government, Individual, or Institution, and avoid anything against caste, creed, or religion that may hurt religious sentiments. Content must remain respectful and non-controversial throughout.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What is the minimum duration requirement for cultural programmes organized under this commemorative scheme?
Answer: The programme duration must be at least 2 hours. This minimum time requirement ensures adequate coverage of the artiste's history and provides sufficient cultural content to honor their legacy properly.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: How many performance venues and shows am I allowed to organize if my application gets approved for this memorial scheme?
Answer: You can organize a maximum of 4 shows at 4 different locations, including 3 shows in cities like Panaji, Margao, Curchorem, or Vasco, and 1 show compulsorily in the deceased artiste's area of residence. Additionally, 2 more village shows may be granted subject to fund availability.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What specific information about the honored artiste must be included as part of every commemorative programme under this scheme?
Answer: The programme must compulsorily include narration of the complete history and life story of the late artiste to whom the programme is dedicated. This biographical content is essential for educating the audience about their contributions.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: Do I need to invite specific people to attend the commemorative function, and are there any mandatory guests required?
Answer: Family members of the deceased artiste must be compulsorily invited to the function. Additionally, the President or Vice President of the Tiatr Academy of Goa will serve as either the Chief Guest or Guest of Honour at your event.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What acknowledgment requirements must I follow in all promotional materials and advertisements for my commemorative cultural programme?
Answer: All advertisements, whether oral, print, electronic media, or banners, must include the phrase "This programme is held in collaboration with Tiatr Academy of Goa." This acknowledgment is mandatory across all promotional activities and materials.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What banner and logo display requirements do I need to follow during Tiatr performances versus Musical Shows?
Answer: For Tiatr performances, you must display the Tiatr Academy of Goa's banner on the front side wing of the stage and return it afterward. For Musical Shows, display a minimum 6ft x 10ft banner carrying the Tiatr Academy logo as backdrop.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What financial documentation and receipts do I need to submit after completing my commemorative programme to receive reimbursement?
Answer: You must submit a statement of expenditure with all original bills enclosed. If any bill exceeds ₹5,000/-, you need a stamped receipt. This financial documentation is required for benefit disbursement and audit purposes.

Scheme: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
Question: What photographic evidence and records do I need to provide to the Academy after completing my commemorative cultural programme?
Answer: You must send 5 copies of photographs from the function to the Tiatr Academy of Goa for their records. Two of these photographs must specifically show the Tiatr Academy banner prominently displayed during the performance.

Scheme: Tiatr Research Scholarship Program

Scheme: Tiatr Research Scholarship Program

Scheme: Tiatr Research Scholarship Program

Scheme: Tiatr Research Scholarship Program

Scheme: Tiatr Research Scholarship Program

Scheme: Tiatr Research Scholarship Program

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
**Step 1:** Access the official [National Testing Agency portal](https://www.nta.ac.in/) and register for National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA. Complete the registration process by providing personal details, educational qualifications, and uploading required documents including caste certificate and income certificate.
**Step 2:** Take the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA conducted by National Testing Agency across the country. The test will assess merit for admission to SHRESHTA schools and results will determine eligibility for school selection process.

**Step 3:** After the examination, check the results on National Testing Agency portal to verify qualification status and merit position. Qualified candidates will be eligible to participate in the web counselling process for school selection.
**Step 4:** Access the web counselling system developed by National Informatics Centre to exercise choice of SHRESHTA schools. Select preferred schools from the available options based on merit rank and availability of seats in chosen institutions.
**Step 5:** Once a school is allotted through the counselling process, confirm the selection within the stipulated time frame. The selected school will automatically admit the student without any further test or evaluation process.

**Step 6:** Report to the assigned SHRESHTA school and complete all admission formalities as directed by the school authorities. The school will provide necessary assistance for students to settle down in the new environment and hostel facilities.
**Step 7:** Participate in the bridge course conducted by the school outside school hours if required. The bridge course will cover topics to help catch up with the rest of the class and enhance capability to adapt to the school environment.
##### ***Selection Process***

- The applicant will be selected based on merit obtained in National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA.
- The applicant will be offered choices of SHRESHTA schools through web counselling system.
- The applicant may participate in multiple rounds of web-counselling to ensure all seats are filled.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: What is the maximum annual family income limit for students applying under this residential education program for Scheduled Caste students?
Answer: The parental income shall not exceed ₹2,50,000/- per year for eligibility under this scheme.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: Which classes can students apply for admission and what are the academic prerequisites for each level in this quality education initiative?
Answer: Students can apply for admission in Class 9th after passing Class 8th in the immediately preceding academic year, or for Class 11th after passing Class 10th in the immediately preceding academic year.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: How much financial assistance is provided annually for each class under this scholarship program for residential schooling?
Answer: The scholarship amounts are Class 9th: ₹1,00,000/-, Class 10th: ₹1,10,000/-, Class 11th: ₹1,25,000/-, and Class 12th: ₹1,35,000/- per student per annum covering school fee and hostel fee.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: What is the selection process and testing mechanism for students seeking admission to these premier private residential institutions?
Answer: Students must qualify through the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA conducted by National Testing Agency, followed by merit-based selection and web counselling for school choice.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: How many seats are allocated annually across the country for fresh admissions under this educational opportunity program?
Answer: The tentative allocation provides 1500 seats in Class 9th and 1500 seats in Class 11th each year from 2023-24 to 2025-26, totaling 3000 fresh admissions annually.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: Can students already receiving benefits under other scholarship schemes of the department apply for this residential education program?
Answer: Students applying under this scheme should not be covered under Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: What type of schools are recognized and selected under this initiative for providing quality education to Scheduled Caste students?
Answer: The best performing private residential schools are selected based on Central Board of Secondary Education database, schools recommended by District Authorities, and other eligible private residential schools affiliated to State or Central Boards.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: What additional academic support is provided to help students adapt to the new learning environment in these institutions?
Answer: A bridge course may be conducted outside school hours covering academic topics and personality development, with funding up to 10% of annual fee for up to 3 months duration.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: How long will students continue to receive financial support once they are admitted under this residential education scheme?
Answer: Students admitted in Class 9 or 11 shall automatically be funded for the next classes till they complete 12th class, subject to passing the exams of the previous class.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: What are the minimum operational requirements and infrastructure standards that participating schools must maintain under this program?
Answer: Schools should have existed for at least 5 years, maintain more than 75% pass percentage in Class 10 and 12 for the last 3 years, and have adequate infrastructure for admitting at least 10 additional Scheduled Caste students.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: Within what timeframe are the scholarship funds transferred directly to the selected schools after student admission confirmation?
Answer: The fee covering school fee and hostel fee would be released directly to schools by the Ministry within 30 days from the date of confirmation of admission on the Information Technology portal.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: What happens if a student decides to leave the school after admission and fee payment has been made to the institution?
Answer: If any student leaves after getting admitted and payment of fee to the school, it should be brought to notice of Central Government immediately and fees paid should be refunded to the Consolidated Fund of India.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: Are there any charges or fees that students need to pay directly to the schools under this residential education program?
Answer: No fee or any other charges will be charged from the beneficiary by the schools participating in this scheme as all costs are covered by the scholarship amount.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 1 - SHRESHTA Schools (Best CBSE Private Residential Schools)
Question: What counselling and support mechanisms are available for students to help them settle in their new residential school environment?
Answer: Schools designate one of the teachers as counsellor who would resolve difficulties faced by students and provide necessary assistance to settle down in the new environment.

are required.1. Poisonous Substances: First Information Report (FIR)/Police Report, Post Mortem Report, Viscera Report, Forensic Lab Report, and Death Certificate.1. Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: What is the scheme is about?
Answer: The Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) that provides insurance coverage to fishers, fish workers, fish farmers, and others involved in fishing-related activities

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: What does the Accidental Death or Permanent Total Disability (PTD) benefit cover?
Answer: The scheme provides a benefit of ₹5,00,000/- for accidental death or permanent total disability.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: What is considered a "Permanent Total Disability" under this scheme?
Answer: Permanent Total Disability is defined as an injury that, within 12 months of the accident, is the sole and direct cause of the insured person being permanently, totally, and absolutely disabled from engaging in any occupation or employment.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: Who is eligible for this benefit?
Answer: Eligible individuals are men and women fishers between the ages of 18 and 70, as approved by the State/UT fisheries department. The insured person must not have completed 71 years of age on the date of the accident.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: What is the policy's duration?
Answer: The insurance cover is valid for a period of 12 months.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: How is the premium paid for the insurance?
Answer: The entire premium amount is paid by the Central and State Governments, with no contribution from the beneficiary.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: How do I report a claim for accidental death or permanent total disability?
Answer: The claim must be intimated to M/s Oriental Insurance Company Limited (OICL) within 90 days from the date of the accident.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: What documents are required to file a claim?
Answer: Common documents include the Intimation Form, Claim Form, a cancelled cheque or bank passbook copy, Certification by an Appropriate Authority, and a government-issued ID. Additional documents, such as the First Information Report (FIR) and Post Mortem Report, are required for specific accidents.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: Where do I submit the claim documents?
Answer: All hard copies of the insurance claim documents should be sent to the Insurance Cell at the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) after being uploaded to the PMMSY-GAIS MIS Portal.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: How long does it take for a claim to be settled?
Answer: The insurance company will settle a claim within 15 working days of receiving all complete documentation.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: What happens if the insurance company delays the claim payment?
Answer: If an admissible claim is not settled within 15 days, the insurance company will pay a simple interest of 10% on the claim amount from the date of document submission until the date of payment.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: Will the claim be paid to the family or the insured person?
Answer: The payment is made directly to the claimant, nominee, or legal heir's savings account via Direct Bank Transfer (DBT).

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: Are there any exclusions to the accidental death or PTD coverage?
Answer: Yes, the policy does not cover death or disability resulting from suicide, self-inflicted injury, pre-existing conditions, drug or alcohol use, criminal acts, or war. Natural death is also not covered.

Scheme: Group Accident Insurance Scheme under PMMSY: Accidental death or Permanent Total Disability Gujarat
Question: What is the role of the State/UT Fisheries Department in the claims process?
Answer: The State/UT department is responsible for identifying and verifying the fishers to be insured, forwarding claim intimations, and ensuring all claim documents are verified and submitted on time.

Scheme: Gaura Shakti Yojana
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
In view of the safety of women and the prompt redressal of their complaints, the “Gaura Shakti Module” has been developed under the Uttarakhand Police App. After registration, the registrant remains in direct one-to-one contact with the designated Women Police Officer of the concerned police station. For effective implementation, a detailed SOP has been prepared, and all concerned officials have been trained at the headquarters level. In addition, a separate mobile number has been allotted to the in-charges of Women Help Desks in all police stations. Through this app, women can also easily register complaints online.
To ensure 24×7 accessibility, the Police Department has made the following platforms available for reporting crimes against women/girls or for registering complaints:

1. Dial 112 – with trained female police personnel available round-the-clock.
 1. WhatsApp number at Police Headquarters – 9411112780
 1. “Women Help Desk” at every police station.
 1. Uttarakhand Police App – “Gaura Shakti Module” / SOS feature
 1. Police station / outpost

With the objective of making every police station in the state more women-friendly, at least one Woman Sub-Inspector and four Women Constables have been deployed at each police station.

- The Uttarakhand Police also ensures payment of compensation amounts as per rules under the Crime Victim Assistance Scheme, 2013. Further, the Uttarakhand Sexual Crime and Other Crimes Victim/Survivor Women Compensation Scheme, 2020 has been implemented for women victims. All concerned officials have been directed to assist crime victims in obtaining compensation under both schemes and to coordinate with the concerned departments as required.

- Keeping in mind the sensitivity of cases involving women, investigations of sexual crimes against women are conducted exclusively by Women Officers. To ensure quality investigations, a booklet containing detailed SOPs and instructions has been issued by the headquarters and distributed to all women investigators. For scientific evidence collection in such cases, Sexual Assault Evidence Collection (SAEC) Kits are being provided to districts as needed.
 - Cases registered under POCSO and rape are being disposed of within the prescribed timelines. According to the ITSSO Portal, Uttarakhand ranks third at the national level in the timely disposal of such cases within two months.

- Under the provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) has been constituted in each district under the chairmanship of the Senior Superintendent of Police. Additionally, a Child Welfare Police Officer (CWPO) has been appointed at every police station. Child-friendly police stations have also been established in every district.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
- In the event of death, serious injury, or disability caused by a wild animal, 30% of the total compensation amount payable for the incident will be provided to the victim or dependent as an advance. This will be based on the confirmation of the incident by the village head of the affected area, any currently serving public representative, and the forest guard of the concerned area. The advance will be provided within a maximum of 48 hours (excluding public holidays) from the receipt of information regarding the loss of life or property.

- The remaining amount will be paid upon receipt of the final investigation report. For the payment of the compensation, the Aadhar card, mobile number, and bank account details of the victim or dependent are required.
 - In cases where a person is killed, seriously injured, or disabled by a wild animal, a certificate issued by a state government doctor must be submitted to the office of the concerned Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) or Deputy Director. The DFO/Deputy Director will then have full authority to approve or release the ex-gratia payment based on the final investigation report prepared by the concerned Assistant Conservator of Forests or Wildlife Warden. The DFO/Deputy Director will also forward complete details of the case to the Chief Wildlife Warden.

- The final investigation report must be submitted within 15 days of the incident. Before making the final payment of the ex-gratia amount, a certificate will be obtained from the Revenue Department regarding the dependents of the deceased. If the final investigation report does not confirm that the victim was killed, seriously injured, or disabled by a wild animal, the advance amount paid to the victim or dependent will be recovered as revenue.

**Note:** The Forest Department has issued a toll-free number, 1800-890-9715, where any person can report human-wildlife incidents or the presence of wildlife in populated areas anywhere in the state.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Question: What types of incidents are covered under this scheme?
Answer: The scheme covers death, serious injury, or permanent disability caused by attacks from wild animals such as tigers, leopards, snow leopards, wild elephants, bears, hyenas, wild boars, crocodiles/gharial, snakes, and other specified species in and around forest areas.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Question: Who is eligible to claim compensation?
Answer: The victim or their legal dependents are eligible to claim compensation. Family members or others cannot claim if the victim was an old person, medically unfit, handicapped, mentally unbalanced, or a minor left alone in the forest.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Question: How is the advance payment provided?
Answer: 30% of the total payable amount is provided as an advance within a maximum of 48 hours (excluding public holidays) from the receipt of information about the incident.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Question: Who approves the final ex-gratia payment?
Answer: The Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) or Deputy Director approves or releases the ex-gratia amount based on the final investigation report prepared by the Assistant Conservator of Forests/Wildlife Warden.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Question: Within how many days is the final investigation report submitted?
Answer: The final investigation report is prepared and submitted within 15 days of the incident.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Question: What is the procedure if a person is seriously injured by a wild animal?
Answer: The victim must obtain a certificate from a state government doctor and submit it to the Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director, who will process the compensation based on the investigation report.

Scheme: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
Question: How can incidents be reported?
Answer: Incidents can be reported through the toll-free number of the Forest Department: 1800 890 9715.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
**Step 1:****** ***Registration and Application Submission***

- Organizations must register on the NGO Darpan portal and get a project ID from the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.
- Submit your application on the e-Anudaan portal between April 1st and June 30th.
- Include all required details for your organization, project, and students (both new and renewals).

**Step 2:****** ***Document Preparation and Submission***

**Step 2:****** ***Document Preparation and Submission***

- Gather and submit key documents like project details, budget, and previous year's performance reports.
- Upload all necessary forms to the e-Anudaan portal.
- While state government recommendations are ideal, applications may still be considered after a project inspection.

**Step 3:****** ***Physical Inspection and Verification***

- A team from the Ministry's Programme Management Unit will inspect your organization.
- The inspection, preferably during the first academic quarter, will assess your infrastructure and performance.
- Continued grant support depends on demonstrating satisfactory performance and adherence to all scheme guidelines.

**Step 4:****** ***Agreement and Bank Account Setup***

**Step 4:****** ***Agreement and Bank Account Setup***

- You must sign an Agreement Bond to receive assistance.
- Set up a joint-operation bank account for electronic fund transfers.
- All bank account details must be verified through the Public Financial Management System before funds can be released.

**Step 5:****** ***Grant Release and Ongoing Compliance***

- Grants are released in three installments after the application is complete and the inspection report is submitted.
- Maintain separate accounts for scheme grants and submit utilization certificates to continue receiving funding.
- Your organization is required to maintain proper records and provide real-time updates on your website and the e-Anudaan portal.

***Application Deadlines:*** Portal opens on 1st April for renewal students and closes on 30th June for fresh student entries annually.
***Application Status Tracking:*** Status can be tracked through e-Anudaan portal at www.grants-msje.gov.in with real-time data management information system integration.
***Grievance Redressal / Help & Support:*** Applications and queries to be addressed through e-Anudaan portal www.grants-msje.gov.in under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment supervision.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: What type of organizations are eligible to receive grant-in-aid for running schools under this educational assistance program?
Answer: The organization must be a reputed school chain, Corporate Social Responsibility foundation, or reputed organization running good quality schools recognized by the State Government and affiliated to State or Central Boards. Additionally, the organization must be registered on the Non-Governmental Organization Darpan portal of National Institution for Transforming India Aayog.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: How much financial assistance can our organization receive per Scheduled Caste student annually for residential school operations?
Answer: For primary level residential schools, organizations receive ₹44,000/- per Scheduled Caste student per year, while for secondary level residential schools, the assistance is ₹55,000/- per Scheduled Caste student per year.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: What happens if the attendance of Scheduled Caste students in our school falls below 75% during inspection?
Answer: If attendance is between 50% to less than 75%, you will receive 75% of the grant amount. If attendance is between 25% to less than 50%, only 50% grant will be provided. If attendance falls below 25% without valid grounds, no grant-in-aid will be released.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: Are there any additional non-recurring grants available for infrastructure development and how frequently can we apply for them?
Answer: Yes, non-recurring grants are available every 5 years for infrastructure items. For example, a secondary residential school accommodating 100 students can receive ₹3,85,000/- for fixed items plus ₹900/- per student for items like furniture, bedding material, laboratory equipment, and Closed Circuit Television installation.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: What minimum academic performance standards must our school maintain to continue receiving grant-in-aid under this program?
Answer: Your school must maintain Class 10th and Class 12th pass percentage that is not less than the average Board result of the respective State or Central Board. Teachers must also be qualified graduates with Bachelor of Education qualification for high schools.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: Do we need to maintain separate financial accounts for the grants received and what are the auditing requirements?
Answer: Yes, you must maintain separate accounts for grants received under this program, which shall always be open for inspection by Government officers or Comptroller and Auditor General. You must also submit audited statement of accounts with utilization certificate after each financial year closure.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: What infrastructure facilities are mandatory for residential schools to qualify for grant-in-aid and maintain funding eligibility?
Answer: Essential infrastructure includes one classroom per class, adequate furniture for all students, one decent cot and bed per child, proper lighting and fans, hygienic toilets at ratio of 1:10 children, hygienic kitchen and dining facilities, clean drinking water, medical facilities with regular doctor visits, and Closed Circuit Television installation with live streaming capability.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: How many installments will our organization receive annually and what is the process for fund release?
Answer: Grants are released in three installments per year after submission of complete proposal and Programme Management Unit inspection report. Funds are transferred electronically directly to your organization's bank account through the e-Anudaan portal.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: What are the consequences if our organization provides false information or fails to comply with the terms and conditions?
Answer: If false information is provided or unethical practices are found, your organization will be blacklisted and this information will be communicated to National Institution for Transforming India Aayog for removal from Non-Governmental Organization Darpan portal. You may also be required to refund grants with 12% interest.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: Can organizations charging any fees from beneficiary students still qualify for grant-in-aid under this educational support program?
Answer: No capitation fees or donations can be charged from beneficiaries. If any fee is collected, it must be declared in accounts furnished to the Ministry and the corresponding amount will be deducted from the admissible grant-in-aid amount.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: What is the deadline for submitting applications on the e-Anudaan portal and when does the application window open?
Answer: The e-Anudaan portal opens tentatively on 1st April every year for entry of renewal students and remains open till 30th June for entry of fresh students. All required documents and student details must be submitted within this timeframe.

Scheme: Scheme For Residential Education For Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA): Mode 2 - NGO Operated Schools 
Question: Are there any specific teacher qualification requirements and minimum staffing norms that must be maintained throughout the program duration?
Answer: Teachers in high schools must be at least graduates in their respective fields with Bachelor of Education qualification. The minimum number of teachers must not be less than 6 in a school and not less than 2 in a hostel, with honorariums paid as per minimum district rates.

Scheme: Solo Drama Competition
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
**Step 1:** Visit the official website of 'Mari Yojana' at [https://mariyojana.gujarat.gov.in](https://mariyojana.gujarat.gov.in).
In the search bar provided at the top of the page, type 'Competition'. All the schemes of the Government of Gujarat having the word 'Competition' will be listed.
**Step 2:** From the list, click on the scheme 'Solo Drama Competition'. You will be taken to the schemes page. Navigate and download the application form of the scheme. The application form is available in both Gujarati and English languages, and the applicant should take print of the form in their preferred language.

**Step 3:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 4:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents, within the prescribed period (if any), to the designated authority at the Gujarat State Sangeet Natak Academy.
**Step 5:** After successful submission, the applicant will receive an acknowledgement or reference number. The applicant should save this reference number for future correspondence and tracking of the application status.

> ***Post-Application Processes***

**Step 1:** Once the application is approved, the applicant will be notified about the date, time, and venue of the state-level solo drama competition. The applicant must attend the competition at the scheduled time and perform their solo drama act before the judges.
**Step 2:** After the competition concludes, the results will be evaluated and declared by the organizing committee. Winners will be notified through official channels, and prizes will be distributed to the first and second prize winners, as well as special category award recipients as per the scheme guidelines.

Scheme: Solo Drama Competition

Scheme: Solo Drama Competition

Scheme: Solo Drama Competition

Scheme: Rajya Samekit Sahkari Vikas Yojana - Ganga Gaay Mahila Dairy Yojana
Section: Documents Required
- Aadhaar card
- Bank account details

- Movable/immovable property or land certificate (if applicable)

- Loan details, if any

Scheme: Rajya Samekit Sahkari Vikas Yojana - Ganga Gaay Mahila Dairy Yojana
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
- It is mandatory for the applicant to be a member of the society. Any member above 18 years of age in the concerned Gram Panchayat or rural area can obtain membership by depositing a ₹25.00 membership fee with the nearest society secretary and receiving a receipt. It is not necessary to be a cattle rearer to become a member.

- The application form can be obtained from the milk cooperative society or the nearest district cooperative bank. The form must be submitted along with Aadhaar card, bank account details, caste certificate, cooperative society membership number (if applicable), and movable/immovable property or land certificate. If the above documents are not available, two guarantors who are members of the milk society must be provided.
 - If a loan has been taken from any institution, its details along with the number of animals to be acquired must be submitted to the milk cooperative society. The Society Secretary certifies the application. The Manager/Chief Manager of the Milk Producers Cooperative Union Ltd. and the Assistant Director of Dairy provide recommendations after scrutiny.

- After receiving the recommendations, the application is submitted to the bank. Once the bank verifies all documents, the loan is approved according to the beneficiary’s eligibility, and the loan amount is disbursed to the beneficiary’s account.
 - Upon receiving the funds, the Dairy Cooperative Society/Dairy Department’s Purchase Society informs the beneficiary and accompanies them to purchase animals from department-listed dairy farms outside the state. The Purchase Society selects and purchases the animals, inspects their health, and delivers them to the owner’s home. The owner does not have to pay any money to departmental personnel.

- If the beneficiary is not satisfied with the animals from the listed firm, they must notify the relevant District Manager in writing. After receiving permission, the Purchase Society will provide animals from an alternative source outside the state.

Scheme: Rajya Samekit Sahkari Vikas Yojana - Ganga Gaay Mahila Dairy Yojana

Answer: Women, Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), and general category members of milk-producing cooperative societies are eligible.

**Step 1:** ***Invitation for Project Proposals***

- The National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms, Department of Justice, selects and invites implementing agencies to submit project proposals for subjects that have been identified by the Department.
- This scheme does not follow an open application system but rather focuses on proposals from pre-selected or identified institutes and organisations.

**Step 2:** **Preparation and Submission of the Project Proposal**

**Step 2:** **Preparation and Submission of the Project Proposal**

- The selected implementing agency is required to prepare a comprehensive Project Proposal detailing the terms and conditions of the project, including the objectives, methodology, detailed duration with specific timelines, and a full breakdown of the estimated project cost.
- This complete Project Proposal must be submitted to the National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms, Department of Justice.

**Step 3:** ***Consideration and Final Decision by the Project Sanctioning Committee***

**Step 3:** ***Consideration and Final Decision by the Project Sanctioning Committee***

- All Project Proposals received from the selected institutes and organisations on the identified subjects are systematically placed before the Project Sanctioning Committee for detailed consideration and subsequent approval.
- It is mandated that when the Project Sanctioning Committee deliberates on proposals from the Indian Law Institute or the National Judicial Academy, the Directors of those respective entities shall recuse themselves from the committee's discussions.
- The decision reached by the Project Sanctioning Committee regarding the proposal shall be considered final and binding on all parties.

**Step 4:** ***Financial Approval and Release of Instalments***

**Step 4:** ***Financial Approval and Release of Instalments*** 

- Following the approval by the Project Sanctioning Committee, the Project Proposals are then submitted to the Integrated Finance Division of the Ministry of Law and Justice for final approval of the project and authorization to release the necessary funds. 
- Subsequent financial assistance, which may be given in instalments, shall only be released upon obtaining the explicit approval of the Integrated Finance Division for each specific payment.

**Step 5:** ***Project Execution and Compliance***

**Step 5:** ***Project Execution and Compliance***

- The implementing agency executes the project activity, utilizing the financial assistance received, which is strictly limited to covering the actual expenditure incurred by the grantee institution. 
- Throughout the project, the implementing agency is required to adhere to the duration and specific timelines laid out in the approved Project Proposal for activities such as submitting an interim progress report and making presentations before the submission of the final report.

**Step 6:** ***Submission of Documentation and Final Payment***

**Step 6:** ***Submission of Documentation and Final Payment***

- Upon completion of the project, the implementing agency is required to submit a Utilisation Certificate for the funds received, following the format prescribed by the Department of Justice. 
- The final payment, which constitutes at least 10% of the total project cost, will be released only upon the official acceptance of the final project report by the National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms, Department of Justice.

Scheme: Sheti Samrudhi Yojana
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should take a printout of the [prescribed format](https://goaprintingpress.gov.in/downloads/2526/2526-11-SI-OG-1.pdf) of the application form. Alternatively, the interested applicant should visit the [Zonal Agriculture Officer](https://www.agri.goa.gov.in/ContactUs;jsessionid=8C0446B54FFF58D0E14D99C1661A85D6?0) and request a hard copy of the prescribed format of the application form from the staff.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).

**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents, within the prescribed period (if any), to the Zonal Agriculture Officer.
##### ***Post-Application Processes***
**Step 1:** After verification of the application and all the documents mentioned in the scheme guidelines, the Zonal Agriculture Officer shall forward the complete application package to the Director of Tribal Welfare for final approval and sanction.
**Step 2:** The Director of Tribal Welfare, upon receipt of the application, shall carry out scrutiny of the application form and documents. After satisfactory scrutiny, the Director of Tribal Welfare shall sanction the proposal and the amount to be disbursed to the farmer co-operative society.
##### ***Benefit Disbursement Process***

##### ***Benefit Disbursement Process***
**Step 1:** Fifty percent of the total amount sanctioned shall be disbursed to the farmer’s co-operative society as the first installment.
**Step 2:** The farmer co-operative must submit a utilization certificate for the first installment to the Zonal Agriculture Officer. The Zonal Agriculture Officer shall then monitor the functioning of the Co-operative, verify, sign, and submit the Utilization Certificate to the Director of Tribal Welfare.
**Step 3:** After the Director of Tribal Welfare receives the verified Utilization Certificate of the first installment, the Director shall release the balance amount.

**Step 4:** To avail the benefit for any subsequent year, the farmer co-operative shall submit an annual performance report. This report must be verified, signed, and recommended by the concerned Zonal Agriculture Officer. If the report is not submitted, the succeeding year benefit will be kept on hold until the report is furnished by the co-operative.
