Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
**Step 1:** Visit the [Official Website](https://nlm.udyamimitra.in/) of "National Livestock Mission" and click "[Apply Here](https://nlm.udyamimitra.in/Login/Login)".
**Step 2:** The following methods of Logging In will be displayed:

- Login as Entrepreneur
- Login as Government / Other Agencies
- Login as Research & Innovation

- Login as Entrepreneur
- Login as Government / Other Agencies
- Login as Research & Innovation

Login to the website using your preferred method.
**Step 3:** On the next page, verify your Mobile Number via OTP. You will be taken to the Online Application Form. 
**Step 4:** In the form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload all the mandatory documents in the specified format and size.
**Step 5:** Agree to the "Declaration & Authorization" by ticking the checkbox. Provide the Date & Place, and finally click "Submit".
> **Post-Application Processes**

**Step 1:** **Screening of application by State Implementing Agency (SIA)**
SIA will scrutinize the submitted application and will recommend the application of the entrepreneurs/ eligible entities to avail balance financing for the project through scheduled banks or financial institutions like National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) etc.
**Step 2:** **Loan sanction by Lender**

**Step 2:** **Loan sanction by Lender**
After the recommendation of the project by SIA, the same will be considered by the bank or financial institutions for financing. Lender will pick the application along with all the documents from the portal and will approve the loan after examining the project/ documents submitted by applicant and completing their internal deligent process. After sanctioning the loan, Lender will upload sanction letter on the portal.
**Step 3:** **Recommendation from State Level Executive Committee (SLEC)**
Once the bank or financial institution sanction the project, SIA shall place the same in SLEC for recommending the application to the Central Government (Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying).
**Step 4:** **Approval of subsidy by DAHD**

**Step 4:** **Approval of subsidy by DAHD**
DAHD will approve the subsidy and will mark the approval of the same on portal.
**Step 5:** **Disbursement and release of subsidy**
After compliance of terms and conditions mentioned in the sanction letter, lender will disburse the loan amount to the beneficiary. fund the subsidy amount for the approved projects through Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to the lending Bank or financial institutions as the case may be to release the subsidy to Beneficiaries.
> **Track Application Status**

> You can check your application status from the "[TRACK STATUS](https://www.nlm.udyamimitra.in/Login/Login)" tab available in the upper right corner of the portal

> **Help and Support**

> If you encounter any issues or have questions, visit the "[Contact Us](https://nlm.udyamimitra.in/Home/Contact)" page.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry

Answer: Individuals, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Farmers Producer Organizations (FPOs), Farmers Cooperatives (FCOs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), and Section 8 companies can apply.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: How is the subsidy disbursed?
Answer: For bank-financed projects, the subsidy is released in two installments—first after the loan disbursement and confirmation, and second after project completion and verification.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: Is the scheme available for self-financed projects?
Answer: Yes, self-financed projects are eligible, but applicants must provide a bank guarantee valid for three years for the remaining project cost beyond the subsidy amount.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: What kind of poultry can be reared under this scheme?
Answer: Only Low Input Technology Birds or those that can be sustained in a free-range management system are permitted.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: What are the essential project components covered under this scheme?
Answer: Parent Farms, Rural Hatcheries, and Brooder cum Mother Units with a minimum of 1,000 parent layers are covered.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: How long does it take for the second installment of the subsidy to be released?
Answer: The second instalment is released after project completion and verification by the State Implementing Agency.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: Who verifies the project for subsidy disbursement?
Answer: The State Implementing Agency verifies the project and confirms eligibility for the second instalment of the subsidy.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: Can private organizations supply birds for the scheme?
Answer: Yes, private organizations with certificates of guaranteed production, along with designated research institutions, can supply birds.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
Question: What documents are required for application?
Answer: Applicants must provide identity proof, address proof, business entity registration, a detailed project report, bank loan approval (if applicable), a bank guarantee (for self-financing), and a declaration form.

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry

Scheme: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
**Step 1:** The eligible units had to register with the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce using the prescribed proforma/form.
**Step 2:** Submit half-yearly claims covering January-June and July-December periods. Claims had to be filed within 3 months of the half-yearly period (first half-year claim by 30th September, second half-year claim by 31st March).
**Step 3:** The Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce scrutinized and prepared a list of eligible units and forwarded it to the Task Force Committee within one month. The Task Force Committee verified claims and finalized the list within two months.
_*Any disputes could be filed with the Chief Secretary, whose decision was final._

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: As a business owner considering applying for an industrial subsidy program that was available previously, I'd like to know what percentage of local employees was required to qualify?
Answer: The scheme required units to employ 80% local manpower to qualify for the subsidy. It's important to note that contract workers, temporary workers, and daily wage employees were not considered when calculating this percentage.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: Could you please explain the employment criteria in detail, specifically regarding which relatives couldn't be counted as employees for an industrial subsidy program I applied for in Goa?
Answer: Proprietor, partner, promoters, directors, or their relatives were not considered employees for subsidy claims. This included spouse, father, mother, son/daughter, grandparent, son-in-law, daughter-in-law, brother, sister, and first cousin of the business owners or directors.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: I'm a female entrepreneur who owned a manufacturing unit in Goa around 2009-2010. Were there any special preferences or priorities given to women-owned businesses under the subsidy scheme?
Answer: Yes, the scheme gave preference to women-owned proprietary concerns with 100% ownership by women, and partnership firms where 51% ownership was held by women, provided there was at least one additional partner other than husband, father, brother, or son.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: What were the environmental category requirements for manufacturing businesses to qualify for the industrial employment subsidy that was offered in Goa a few years ago?
Answer: Under the scheme, units had to fall under Green, Orange, or specified Orange categories of environmental classification to be eligible. Units in other environmental categories were not eligible for the subsidy.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: Could you explain the different subsidy rates that were available for new manufacturing units located in developed versus less developed talukas in Goa under a previous subsidy program?
Answer: For new units in developed talukas, a 25% subsidy was provided. New units in less developed talukas received an additional 10% subsidy, bringing their total to 35%. The total subsidy could not exceed 40% including all additional benefits.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: As an owner of an existing small manufacturing enterprise in a less developed taluka of Goa, what subsidy percentage would I have been eligible for under the employment scheme that ended in 2011?
Answer: Existing micro and small units in less developed talukas were eligible for a 15% subsidy (10% base subsidy plus an additional 5% for being in a less developed taluka). This was subject to the overall ceiling of 40% including all additional benefits.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: My manufacturing unit was declared sick but had a revival plan in place. What level of subsidy could I have claimed under the Goa industrial subsidy scheme that operated until March 2011?
Answer: For sick units under a revival plan, the subsidy was defined by the appropriate authority, subject to a maximum of 25%. You would have needed to provide the revival plan approval documentation when applying.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: What additional benefits were available under the local employment subsidy component of the industrial scheme that operated in Goa between 2008 and 2011?
Answer: The scheme offered a 5% additional benefit under the Local Employment Subsidy Scheme, preference in Capital Contribution and under Special Capital Contribution Schemes, and increased interest subsidy limits.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: Could you please clarify the interest subsidy benefits that were available to qualifying manufacturing units under the Goa industrial subsidy program that operated until March 2011?
Answer: The scheme increased interest subsidy limits from 1% to 2% of turnover, with 35% of interest paid (up from 30%), subject to an overall ceiling of [?]8,00,000/-. This was one of several additional benefits available to qualifying units.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: What documents were required to prove that my employees qualified as "local manpower" under the Goa industrial subsidy scheme that operated between 2008 and 2011?
Answer: You needed to provide a declaration executed before a Magistrate regarding employee eligibility, and from January 1st, 2009, Green Social Security Cards for employees were required as proof of their status as local manpower.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: Could you explain the complete application process for the manufacturing subsidy scheme that was available in Goa, from initial registration through to approval and disbursement?
Answer: Eligible units had to register with the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce using the prescribed form, submit half-yearly claims within 3 months of each period, undergo scrutiny by the Task Force Committee, and then receive approval for disbursement of benefits.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: What was the role and composition of the Task Force Committee that evaluated applications for the industrial subsidy scheme in Goa that operated until March 2011?
Answer: The Task Force Committee comprised the General Manager of the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce (as Chairman), Assistant Director (Adm.), Under Secretary (Finance/Expenditure), and representatives from the Goa Chamber of Commerce and industry associations. The committee verified claims and finalized the list of beneficiaries.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
Question: What was the expected timeframe for processing and disbursement of claims under the Goa employment subsidy scheme once all documentation was submitted correctly?
Answer: The Directorate had one month to prepare the list of eligible units, the Task Force Committee had two months to verify claims, and disbursement was made within 15 days of claim finalization, making the total process approximately 3.5 months.

Scheme: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008

Answer: As a medium-sized unit, you needed approval from the High Powered Coordination Committee issued after 1st April 2008 to be eligible for the scheme, in addition to meeting all other criteria like the 80% local employment requirement.

Scheme: Gujarat Textile Policy: Assistance for Saving in Consumption of Energy and Water

Scheme: Gujarat Textile Policy: Assistance for Saving in Consumption of Energy and Water

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: What is the purpose of this scheme?
Answer: The purpose of this scheme is to provide financial relief to sugar cooperative societies by subsidizing the interest on loans taken for clearing sugarcane arrears for the 2018-19 season.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
Answer: Only sugar cooperative societies that have taken a bank loan to pay sugarcane arrears for the 2018-19 season are eligible to apply.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: What kind of financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
Answer: The scheme provides interest subvention for a maximum period of 4 years. The Government of India pays the first year's interest, while the state government provides a subsidy of up to 7% or the actual interest paid, whichever is lower, for the remaining period.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: Can private sugar mills apply for this scheme?
Answer: No, only sugar cooperative societies are eligible under this scheme. Private sugar mills do not qualify for the benefits.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: What is the maximum duration for which interest subvention is provided?
Answer: The interest subvention is provided for a maximum period of four years or until the loan is fully repaid, whichever comes earlier.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: Can a sugar cooperative society apply for this scheme if it has already repaid the loan?
Answer: No, the scheme is applicable only for ongoing loans taken for sugarcane arrears of the 2018-19 season. Societies that have already repaid their loans are not eligible for interest subvention.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: Can a sugar cooperative society apply for multiple loans under this scheme?
Answer: No, a sugar cooperative society can avail of interest subvention only for a single loan taken for clearing sugarcane arrears of the 2018-19 season.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: How is the interest subvention amount calculated?
Answer: The interest subvention amount is calculated based on the actual interest paid on the loan or 7%, whichever is lower, for a maximum period of four years or until the loan is repaid.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)
Question: What is the process for applying under this scheme?
Answer: Eligible sugar cooperative societies must submit their proposals through the District Registrar of the concerned district. The proposal is then forwarded to the Director of Sugar, Gujarat State, Gandhinagar, for approval.

Scheme: Interest Subvention against long terms loan to the Co-operative sugar societies (Normal Area) (Tribal Area)

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: What is the primary objective of this Scheme?
Answer: The primary objective of the scheme is to promote farm mechanization by providing financial assistance to eligible groups and individuals, ensuring that farmers have access to essential agricultural equipment and reducing the cost of farming.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: Who is eligible to apply for the AGR-61 Agro Service Providers Scheme?
Answer: The scheme is open to Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies (PACS), Farmer Groups, Farmer Producer Companies, Cooperative Institutions, Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Sakhi Mandals, and individuals with relevant agricultural education such as a Diploma, Graduate, or Postgraduate degree in Agriculture or a Bachelor of Rural Studies (B.R.S.).

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: How much financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
Answer: The scheme provides financial assistance of up to 75% of the cost of farm implements (limited to [?]7,50,000/-) in general areas and up to 85% (limited to [?]8,50,000/-) in tribal areas.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: How is the financial assistance distributed over the years?
Answer: In general areas, the assistance is provided as 40% in the first year, 10% in the second and third years, and 7.5% in the fourth and fifth years. In tribal areas, the assistance is 50% in the first year, 10% in the second and third years, and 7.5% in the fourth and fifth years.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: Can an individual farmer apply for the scheme?
Answer: An individual farmer can apply only if they hold an agricultural qualification such as a Diploma, Graduate, or Postgraduate degree in Agriculture or a Bachelor of Rural Studies (B.R.S.). Otherwise, only eligible groups and cooperative institutions can apply.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: Are cooperative institutions eligible for this scheme?
Answer: Yes, cooperative institutions engaged in agriculture are eligible to apply under this scheme.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: Can an SHG (Self-Help Group) or Sakhi Mandal apply for the scheme?
Answer: Yes, registered Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Sakhi Mandals can apply for financial assistance under this scheme.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: Is the scheme applicable to farmers outside Gujarat?
Answer: No, the AGR-61 Agro Service Providers Scheme is exclusively for farmers and agricultural entities within Gujarat.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: Where can an applicant submit their application?
Answer: The application must be submitted online through the iKhedut Portal at https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in.

Scheme: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
Question: How are applications processed under the scheme?
Answer: Applications are processed on a first-come, first-serve basis, subject to the availability of funds and the target limits set under the scheme.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What is the objective of this scheme?
Answer: The “Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities” under the “SAIP for MSMEs” scheme, aims to provide one time back-ended incentive for development of Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities based on land area.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
Answer: Any private sector having minimum 5 acre land under its legal possession (by direct purchase, or on lease from the State Govt) can apply through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered under Companies Act/Societies Registration Act /Partnership Act/LLP can apply for setting up a new Industrial Park on the said land.
Also, Owner of any existing/operational privately operated.
industrial parks can also apply under SAIP, provided:-
a) Park area is expanded up to minimum 5 acre in outlying districts and minimum 2 acre in Kolkata and Howrah.
b) The individual units have complied with all the necessary clearances for land conversion, fire licence, environmental issues, building plan etc.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What is the minimum size of land for a Park under SAIP?
Answer: Minimum area required for a Park with for heterogeneous activities is 5 acre in any district.
However, the scheme shall also be extended to parks dedicated entirely/substantially for Logistics and Warehousing Industry. But such parks shall have to be set up outside the municipal limits and must be developed upon a minimum area of 10 acres.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What is the role of SPV?
Answer: SPV will develop the Master Plan/Layout plan of the AIP adhering to the Urban Planning/ Town & Country Planning rules and shall have to obtain the master plan/ layout plan approval from relevant State Government Department with respect to adherence of rules (FAR, Land use, Area Statement, Open Space, Fire Safety, Waste water Management, Water Conservation, Drainage, Sewerage, Solid Waste Disposal, Utility shifting, Power, water, telecommunication, road connectivity and network, etc) including conformation of specification of infrastructure facilities/utilities and quality standard.

The SPV shall also be responsible for compliance of other statutory norms (Consent to Establish for the Park based on the activities of the proposed Units envisaged, Mutation, Conversion, Exemption of 14Y of WBLR/ UC Acts, if applicable, etc) as relevant from concerned State Government Departments/Govt. of India/ Authorities. All the compliances/ approvals/ licenses shall have to be obtained before construction of the park.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What does Legal Possession of any land mean?
Answer: The basic requirement of legal possession is completion of Mutation process for the proposed land in f/o the SPV, or, in favour of the proponent individuals. For the latter, the said individuals have to make a Development agreement with the SPV giving it liberty to develop the Park upon their land.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What are the basic and common infrastructural facilities to be installed in the AlP?
Answer: Common infrastructural facilities mean anything that will be used commonly by the MSME units in the park. Examples are - Land development, boundary walls, internal roads and street lighting, storm water drainage, sewerage system, STP & WTP (if applicable), water distribution network, electrical main distribution network, telecommunication network, common firefighting infrastructure, solid waste disposal site (if applicable), greenery, guardhouse, gate, and misc. civil structure etc.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What is desired manner of land/plot/space allotment to individual units?
Answer: The SPV shall allot the saleable land plot/ space of the ATP to MSMEs through open advertisement in newspapers declaring rates of plot of land/ shed / buildings/ installations. In case applications more than the available plot of land/ shed/ buildings/ installations are received then allotment shall be made through lottery.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What is the minimum number of units to be accommodated in an Approved Industrial Park?
Answer: There shall be minimum 5 number of independent MSME Units in Park which will cover 60% of the allottable area of the park.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What kind of activities are allowed in an AIP?
Answer: Minimum 60% of allottable area can have different manufacturing activities including Cold Storage, Poultry, Fisheries, Logistics & Warehousing.Maximum 5% area can have hostel/housing/guest house.Minimum 10% as open space, or, as per guideline of Building Rule and Ministry of Environment & Forest, Gol.Rest areas can be used for common infrastructure and greenery.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: For how long shall the SPV manage the AIP?
Answer: The SPV shall manage and maintain the AIP for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of completion of construction/installation of the Basic and Essential Common infrastructure Facilities and allotment of minimum 80% of the saleable land to MSMEs without change in shareholding pattern.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
Question: What is the definition of "Approved Industrial Park"?
Answer: Industrial Park for MSMEs approved by "State Level Empowered Committee" (SLEC) under the Scheme and subsequently notified by the State Government in the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What is the objective of this scheme?
Answer: The “Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities” under the “SAIP for MSMEs” scheme, aims to provide one time back-ended incentive for development of Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities based on land area.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
Answer: Any private sector having minimum 5 acre land under its legal possession (by direct purchase, or on lease from the State Govt) can apply through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered under Companies Act/Societies Registration Act /Partnership Act/LLP can apply for setting up a new Industrial Park on the said land.
Also, Owner of any existing/operational privately operated.
industrial parks can also apply under SAIP, provided:-
a) Park area is expanded up to minimum 5 acre in outlying districts and minimum 2 acre in Kolkata and Howrah.
b) The individual units have complied with all the necessary clearances for land conversion, fire licence, environmental issues, building plan etc.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What is the minimum size of land for a Park under SAIP?
Answer: Minimum area required for a Park with for heterogeneous activities is 5 acre in any district.
However, the scheme shall also be extended to parks dedicated entirely/substantially for Logistics and Warehousing Industry. But such parks shall have to be set up outside the municipal limits and must be developed upon a minimum area of 10 acres.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What is the role of SPV?
Answer: SPV will develop the Master Plan/Layout plan of the AIP adhering to the Urban Planning/ Town & Country Planning rules and shall have to obtain the master plan/ layout plan approval from relevant State Government Department with respect to adherence of rules (FAR, Land use, Area Statement, Open Space, Fire Safety, Waste water Management, Water Conservation, Drainage, Sewerage, Solid Waste Disposal, Utility shifting, Power, water, telecommunication, road connectivity and network, etc) including conformation of specification of infrastructure facilities/utilities and quality standard.

The SPV shall also be responsible for compliance of other statutory norms (Consent to Establish for the Park based on the activities of the proposed Units envisaged, Mutation, Conversion, Exemption of 14Y of WBLR/ UC Acts, if applicable, etc) as relevant from concerned State Government Departments/Govt. of India/ Authorities. All the compliances/ approvals/ licenses shall have to be obtained before construction of the park.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What does Legal Possession of any land mean?
Answer: The basic requirement of legal possession is completion of Mutation process for the proposed land in f/o the SPV, or, in favour of the proponent individuals. For the latter, the said individuals have to make a Development agreement with the SPV giving it liberty to develop the Park upon their land.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What are the basic and common infrastructural facilities to be installed in the AlP?
Answer: Common infrastructural facilities mean anything that will be used commonly by the MSME units in the park. Examples are - Land development, boundary walls, internal roads and street lighting, storm water drainage, sewerage system, STP & WTP (if applicable), water distribution network, electrical main distribution network, telecommunication network, common firefighting infrastructure, solid waste disposal site (if applicable), greenery, guardhouse, gate, and misc. civil structure etc.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What is desired manner of land/plot/space allotment to individual units?
Answer: The SPV shall allot the saleable land plot/ space of the ATP to MSMEs through open advertisement in newspapers declaring rates of plot of land/ shed / buildings/ installations. In case applications more than the available plot of land/ shed/ buildings/ installations are received then allotment shall be made through lottery.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What is the minimum number of units to be accommodated in an Approved Industrial Park?
Answer: There shall be minimum 5 number of independent MSME Units in Park which will cover 60% of the allottable area of the park.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What kind of activities are allowed in an AIP?
Answer: - Minimum 60% of allottable area can have different manufacturing activities including Cold Storage, Poultry, Fisheries, Logistics & Warehousing.
 - Maximum 5% area can have hostel/housing/guest house.
 - Minimum 10% as open space, or, as per guideline of Building Rule and Ministry of Environment & Forest, Gol.
 - Rest areas can be used for common infrastructure and greenery.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: For how long shall the SPV manage the AIP?
Answer: The SPV shall manage and maintain the AIP for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of completion of construction/installation of the Basic and Essential Common infrastructure Facilities and allotment of minimum 80% of the saleable land to MSMEs without change in shareholding pattern.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities
Question: What is the definition of "Approved Industrial Park"?
Answer: Industrial Park for MSMEs approved by "State Level Empowered Committee" (SLEC) under the Scheme and subsequently notified by the State Government in the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal.

Scheme: Finance Assistant to PACS for Computerization and Integration of PACS through Core Banking System with District Cooperative Banks

Scheme: Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole

Scheme: Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole

Scheme: Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole

Scheme: Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
Question: What is the objective of the "Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed"?
Answer: The objective of the scheme is to promote the breeding of Gir and Kankrej cows by providing high-quality bulls, thereby improving the quality of calves and gradually increasing milk production in Gujarat.

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
Question: Who can apply for this scheme?
Answer: Only Gram Panchayats and registered Gaushalas under the Charity Act with a minimum of 100 breedable cows are eligible to apply.

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
Question: Can an individual farmer apply for the scheme?

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
Question: What is the minimum requirement for breedable cows to qualify for the scheme?
Answer: The applying organization must have at least 100 breedable cows to qualify for assistance under the scheme.

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
Question: Can neighboring villages combine their cow count to meet the eligibility?
Answer: Yes, if a single village does not have enough breedable cows, neighboring villages can combine their numbers, provided a written guarantee is submitted.

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
Question: What kind of financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
Answer: The scheme provides ₹1,18,000/- in the first year if the bull is supplied by the Board, or ₹1,43,000/- if the bull is purchased by the organization. Additionally, ₹64,800/- is provided for management in the second and third years.

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
Question: For how many years is the assistance provided?

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed

Scheme: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: What is the role of SPV?
Answer: SPV will develop the Master Plan/Layout plan of the AIP adhering to the Urban Planning/ Town & Country Planning rules and shall have to obtain the master plan/ layout plan approval from relevant State Government Department with respect to adherence of rules (FAR, Land use, Area Statement, Open Space, Fire Safety, Waste water Management, Water Conservation, Drainage, Sewerage, Solid Waste Disposal, Utility shifting, Power, water, telecommunication, road connectivity and network, etc) including conformation of specification of infrastructure facilities/utilities and quality standard.

The SPV shall also be responsible for compliance of other statutory norms (Consent to Establish for the Park based on the activities of the proposed Units envisaged, Mutation, Conversion, Exemption of 14Y of WBLR/ UC Acts, if applicable, etc) as relevant from concerned State Government Departments/Govt. of India/ Authorities. All the compliances/ approvals/ licenses shall have to be obtained before construction of the park.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: What does Legal Possession of any land mean?
Answer: The basic requirement of legal possession is completion of Mutation process for the proposed land in f/o the SPV, or, in favour of the proponent individuals. For the latter, the said individuals have to make a Development agreement with the SPV giving it liberty to develop the Park upon their land.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: What are the basic and common infrastructural facilities to be installed in the AlP?
Answer: Common infrastructural facilities mean anything that will be used commonly by the MSME units in the park. Examples are - Land development, boundary walls, internal roads and street lighting, storm water drainage, sewerage system, STP & WTP (if applicable), water distribution network, electrical main distribution network, telecommunication network, common firefighting infrastructure, solid waste disposal site (if applicable), greenery, guardhouse, gate, and misc. civil structure etc.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: What is desired manner of land/ plot/ space allotment to individual units?
Answer: The SPV shall allot the saleable land plot/ space of the ATP to MSMEs through open advertisement in newspapers declaring rates of plot of land/ shed / buildings/ installations. In case applications more than the available plot of land/ shed/ buildings/ installations are received then allotment shall be made through lottery.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: What is the minimum number of units to be accommodated in an Approved Industrial Park?
Answer: There shall be minimum 5 number of independent MSME Units in Park which will cover 60% of the allottable area of the park.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: What kind of activities are allowed in an AIP?
Answer: Minimum 60% of allottable area can have different manufacturing activities including Cold Storage, Poultry, Fisheries, Logistics & Warehousing.Maximum 5% area can have hostel/housing/guest house.Minimum 10% as open space, or, as per guideline of Building Rule and Ministry of Environment & Forest, Gol.Rest areas can be used for common infrastructure and greenery.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: What kind of activities are allowed in an AIP?
Answer: - Minimum 60% of allottable area can have different manufacturing activities including Cold Storage, Poultry, Fisheries, Logistics & Warehousing.
 - Maximum 5% area can have hostel/housing/guest house.
 - Minimum 10% as open space, or, as per guideline of Building Rule and Ministry of Environment & Forest, Gol.
 - Rest areas can be used for common infrastructure and greenery.

Scheme: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Incentive for Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP)
Question: For how long shall the SPV manage the AIP?
Answer: The SPV shall manage and maintain the AIP for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of completion of construction/installation of the Basic and Essential Common infrastructure Facilities and allotment of minimum 80% of the saleable land to MSMEs without change in shareholding pattern.

Scheme: Information, Monitoring, Evaluation and Social Audit (I-MESA): Central Smart Surveillance Unit (CSSU)
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
##### **Step 1:****** ***Initiation of Surveillance Support***

- All divisions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment are required to support the installation of Closed-Circuit Television cameras or electronic devices in Grant-in-aid institutions that receive grants for their schemes. 
- This is a mandatory departmental requirement to facilitate the overall system setup.

##### **Step 2:****** ***Outsourcing Central Monitoring System Implementation***

##### **Step 2:****** ***Outsourcing Central Monitoring System Implementation***

- The responsibility for integrating data from all electronic monitoring devices, providing a complete solution for the Central Monitoring System, developing the required dashboard, and arranging maintenance will be outsourced. 
- This crucial step is undertaken to ensure specialized expertise handles the technological setup.

##### **Step 3:****** ***External Agency Selection and Contract Finalization***

##### **Step 3:****** ***External Agency Selection and Contract Finalization***

- An external agency will be selected through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) utilizing a transparent mechanism to ensure fairness. 
- Following selection, a formal contract will be signed with this external agency specifically covering the setting up of the Central Monitoring System, dashboard development, and ongoing maintenance.

##### **Institutional Compliance Process (Grant-in-aid Institutions)**
##### **Step 1:****** ***Installation of Closed-Circuit Television Devices***

Scheme: Scheme for Construction of Multipurpose Community Halls in Areas Inhabited by Tribal Community (Sanskruti Bhavan)
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
##### **Step 1:****** ***Access the Application Form and Prepare the Proposal***
The applicant, which may be a Village Panchayat, a group of tribals, or a Non-Governmental Organization, must obtain the [prescribed application form](https://goaprintingpress.gov.in/downloads/1213/1213-29-SI-OG.pdf) for Financial Assistance for Construction of Sanskruti Bhavan and finalize the proposed details, including the total estimated cost of the construction.
##### **Step 2:****** ***Gather Supporting Documents and Certifications***

##### **Step 2:****** ***Gather Supporting Documents and Certifications***
The applicant must compile all necessary enclosures required to substantiate the application, including ownership documents for the land, a No Objection Certificate from the land owner (if applicable), and survey records. If the applicant is a group of tribals, they must collect the signatures of at least 100 persons belonging to the tribal community.
##### **Step 3:****** ***Submit the Completed Application to the Department***
The application, along with all required documents, must be submitted to the Tribal Welfare Department in the prescribed manner.
##### **Step 4:****** ***Scrutiny by the Tribal Welfare Department***

##### **Step 4:****** ***Scrutiny by the Tribal Welfare Department***
The Tribal Welfare Department will scrutinize the applications received to check for completeness and adherence to the stated scheme criteria.
##### **Step 5:****** ***Obtain State Level Committee Approval***
The scrutinized application and proposal will be placed before the State Level Committee for final approval; this committee is chaired by the Minister of Tribal Welfare and includes various government officials like the Director of Tribal Welfare and Secretary, Finance.

##### **Post-Application Processes**
##### **Step 1:****** ***Preparation by the Executing Agency***
Upon sanction, the Directorate of Tribal Welfare may get the construction work executed through an Executing Agency. This Executing Agency must ensure that the detailed estimate and drawing of the project are approved by the State Level Committee and that the necessary construction license is obtained.
##### **Step 2:****** ***Release of Funds to the Executing Agency***
The entire cost of the sanctioned project will be deposited with the Executing Agency only after the requirements regarding the estimate, drawing approval, and construction license are fulfilled.
##### **Step 3:****** ***Execute Maintenance Agreement***

##### **Step 3:****** ***Execute Maintenance Agreement***
A separate long term Maintenance Agreement must be entered into with the Executing Agency to govern the maintenance of the Sanskruti Bhavan/Multipurpose Community Hall.
##### **Step 4:****** ***Management and Maintenance Fund Collection***
The local Panchayat will manage the facility and may grant use of the hall at a rate fixed by the Government from time to time; this amount will be credited into the maintenance fund of the hall.

- **Upload Your Papers:** You need to upload pictures or PDF files of your Aadhaar Card, Address Proof, ST Certificate, and a Concept Note (a 3-page letter explaining your business plan). - **Check Everything:** Look over all the pages one last time to make sure there are no mistakes. If you see a mistake, click "Previous" to go back and fix it. - **Submit:** Click the "Submit" button. - **Save Your ID:** A message will pop up with an Application ID. Write this number down! You can use it on the website later to see if your application has been approved or if the officers are still checking your documents.
> **Tracking your Application:** Visit to the [https://ddusyarunachal.in/](https://ddusyarunachal.in/) website and click on the “track your application” to track the application status.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What is the genesis of DDUSY?
Answer: The Government of Arunachal Pradesh launched this startup loan scheme to provide financial assistance via subsidies on loans. It was announced in the State Budget in March 2017 to promote entrepreneurship among unemployed youth through formal banking channels, utilizing the network of scheduled commercial banks across the State.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What is the objective of the scheme?
Answer: The scheme encourages unemployed youth to access low-cost capital for entrepreneurial ventures. It offers 40% front-ended subsidy on project costs from ₹10 L to ₹50 L. Women entrepreneurs get an additional 5% annual interest subsidy, provided the loan doesn’t become a Non-Performing Entity (NPE). Sectors supported include:

- Food processing (agriculture/allied)
- Eco-tourism (homestays, tour operations)
- Traditional textile weaving
- Small manufacturing/bamboo processing/service/diagnostic units
- Other innovative business ideas

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: Who is eligible?
Answer: Unemployed APST (Arunachal Pradesh Scheduled Tribes) entrepreneurs planning to set up new business enterprises are eligible for loans and subsidies.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: Which institution provides loans?
Answer: Any branch of a Scheduled Commercial Bank in Arunachal Pradesh can provide the loan. The loan typically covers 30–50% of project cost (excluding land and building). Entrepreneurs must contribute 10–30% as their own margin; preference is given to higher contributions.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What is the interest rate?
Answer: Rates vary by bank. For State Bank of India (SBI), it’s approximately 3.25–3.50% above EBLR (about 7.55% currently).

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What government support is available?
Answer: Government support includes a 40% front-ended capital investment subsidy under DDUSY. Women entrepreneurs also receive a 5% interest subvention annually, contingent on the account not turning NPE.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What is front-ended capital subsidy?
Answer: This means the subsidy amount is credited upfront to the loan account soon after loan sanction, helping early-stage cashflow.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What is the 5% interest subvention for women beneficiaries?
Answer: If the bank charges 12% interest, a woman entrepreneur would effectively pay 7% after the 5% subvention, in addition to the capital subsidy.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What is margin money/own contribution?
Answer: Applicants must contribute 10–30% of total project cost as their margin. Preference is given to those who contribute more.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: How to apply?
Answer: Applicants must apply via the DDUSY online web portal and prepare a Concept Note/Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the enterprise they wish to establish, then submit it through the portal or the Deputy Commissioner’s Office.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: How are applications processed?
Answer: 1. Scrutiny by District Planning Officer (DPO); CIBIL check by District Lead Bank Manager.
1. District Level Screening Committee (DLSC) meeting chaired by the Deputy Commissioner.
1. Eligible applicants present before DLSC; suitable projects are field-verified.
1. DLSC recommends projects to banks; banks evaluate and sanction viable loans.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What other schemes exist for projects up to ₹10 L?
Answer: Banks can sanction loans below ₹10 L under the Mudra Scheme; visit [www.mudra.org.in](https://www.mudra.org.in/) for details.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What security is required?
Answer: Loans are covered under CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises), so collateral is not insisted upon. If the borrower doesn’t want to bear the guarantee fee, collateral per bank norms is needed.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: What is the repayment tenure?
Answer: Repayment depends on the activity and useful life of assets, not exceeding 7 years, including a moratorium of up to 6 months. Annual reviews are done.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: How to get handholding support?
Answer: The Arunachal Pradesh Innovation and Investment Park (APIIP) in Itanagar provides resources and expertise for startups and new ventures under DDUSY.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: Is plantation activity eligible?
Answer: No. Only value-addition activities under agri-horti and allied sectors are eligible.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: How will banks claim the subsidy?
Answer: Banks scrutinise and sanction loans per their norms, then submit subsidy claims to the Planning & Investment Division with relevant loan details.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
Question: Will government agencies prepare DPRs?
Answer: Applicants must prepare their own DPRs, but they can seek assistance from APIIP or district officials if needed.

Answer: The "Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)" aims to position Gujarat as a global business destination by promoting sustainable manufacturing, inclusive development, and balanced regional growth.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)

Answer: The scheme is effective from August 7, 2020, and will remain in operation until August 6, 2025.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: What is the objective of the component "Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)"?
Answer: The component "Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)" aims to support manufacturing enterprises by providing an interest subsidy on term loans.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
Answer: Any manufacturing enterprise that has taken a term loan from an RBI-regulated bank or financial institution and meets the employment, investment, and compliance conditions is eligible for the subsidy.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: What is the maximum amount of interest subsidy that an enterprise can receive?
Answer: The maximum subsidy amount depends on the category of the taluka:

[?]35 lakhs per annum for Category I talukas.
[?]30 lakhs per annum for Category II talukas.
[?]25 lakhs per annum for Category III talukas and municipal corporation areas.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Can a service sector enterprise apply for this subsidy?
Answer: No, this scheme is specifically designed for enterprises in the manufacturing sector.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Are all term loans eligible for the interest subsidy?
Answer: No, only term loans sanctioned by RBI-regulated banks and financial institutions are eligible. Loans from Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) are not covered under this scheme.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Can an enterprise avail both state and central government interest subsidies?
Answer: Yes, an enterprise can avail of both state and central government subsidies, but the total subsidy received from both sources cannot exceed the total interest paid to the bank or financial institution.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Are existing businesses eligible to apply for the subsidy?
Answer: Yes, existing businesses can apply, particularly if they are investing in expansion, diversification, forward or backward integration, or installing renewable energy solutions.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Does the scheme provide any additional benefits for specific entrepreneurs?
Answer: Yes, the scheme offers an additional 1% interest subsidy for women entrepreneurs, differently-abled entrepreneurs, registered startups, and young entrepreneurs below the age of 35 years.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Will an enterprise continue to receive the subsidy if it defaults on loan repayments?
Answer: No, if an enterprise defaults on interest or loan repayments, the subsidy will not be provided for the default period.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: What happens if an enterprise ceases operations before completing seven years?
Answer: If an enterprise discontinues production within seven years, the subsidy amount disbursed will be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Is it mandatory for an enterprise to comply with pollution control regulations?
Answer: Yes, all enterprises must adhere to the pollution control norms prescribed by the relevant authority, such as the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) or other competent bodies.

Scheme: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
Question: Can an enterprise claim the subsidy for installing a solar power plant?
Answer: Yes, an enterprise installing a solar power plant or other renewable energy systems for captive consumption is eligible for the interest subsidy. However, this incentive is available only once.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: What is Raw Material Assistance Scheme?
Answer: In order to assist the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in procuring the raw material(s), NSIC arranges to provide raw material as per specific needs and requirement of the unit(s).

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: Who can avail assistance under the Scheme?
Answer: Any Manufacturing/Service MSME having Udyam Registration Certificate can apply for the assistance under the Scheme.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: Does NSIC facilitate procurement of raw materials for trading activities?
Answer: No trading activity allowed under Raw Materials Assistance Scheme.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: Does NSIC facilitate MSMEs for raw material procurement against advance payment or on credit?
Answer: NSIC facilitates MSMEs in raw material procurement in both way i.e. against advance payment and also on credit, as per the requirement of MSMEs

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: How to apply for raw material assistance on credit under the Scheme?
Answer: Any MSME needs raw materials through NSIC may apply to any of the NSIC field offices for Raw Material Assistance in the prescribed application forms, which can be downloaded from NSIC's website (www.nsic.co.in) or may be obtained from any of the field offices.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: Where to submit application for raw material assistance?
Answer: The duly filled in application form along with prescribed documents can be submitted with the nearest branch office of NSIC. Details of NSIC offices are available on www.nsic.co.in.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: How the limit is sanctioned for procurement of material on credit?
Answer: A limit is sanctioned keeping in view the raw materials requirements of the unit, financial position of the unit and available security of equivalent value in the form of bank guarantee.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: Whether there is any ceiling of the limit to be sanctioned under the Scheme?
Answer: Maximum exposure to a single unit under the scheme is [?]1000 Lakhs in case of manufacturing unit and [?]600 lakhs in case of service unit. Maximum exposure to an Infrastructure unit will be [?]500 lakhs whether individual or group. The ceiling for maximum exposure to all associate/sister concerns or connected accounts belonging to a 'GROUP' is fixed at [?]2000 lakh for manufacturing units, [?]1500 Lakh for service units and [?]500 Lakh for Infrastructure unit.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: What is the validity of the limits sanctioned under the Scheme?
Answer: One year. Thereafter, the limit can be renewed for one year provided conduct of the account was satisfactory during last year.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: How does NSIC provide credit support to MSMEs for procurement of raw materials?
Answer: The unit has to submit proforma invoice/ original invoice/ material receipt note with the specific request to release the payment. The maximum assistance is provided upto 95% of the Bank Guarantee value.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: Whether payment is released to the MSME?
Answer: No. NSIC releases the payment to the supplier as requested by the MSME.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: What is the credit period of the assistance provided?
Answer: The credit is allowed for 180 days. However, it can further be extended on the request of MSME with the consent of the respective Zonal Head, provided the unit serves interest, the total outstanding is within the Bank Guarantee limit and the Bank Guarantee remains valid for an extended period.

Scheme: Raw Material Assistance Scheme
Question: What are the benefits to MSMEs under the Raw Material Assistance Scheme?
Answer: 1. Materials facilitated under Bulk supply arrangements are provided at the bulk supplier's rate by eliminating the middlemen.
2. Discounts received under bulk supplies arrangements are shared with MSMEs, enabling them to reduce the cost of purchase of materials.
3. Availability of raw material on credit and enabling MSMEs to execute the orders in hand

Scheme: Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY): Strengthening and Up-Gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to Achieve Higher Standards

Answer: Government pharmacies must be licensed under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, GMP certified, provide details of medicines manufactured over the last three years, and propose rational technology and infrastructure upgrades aligned with existing facilities.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: What is CITUS Scheme?
Answer: The scheme "Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme (CITUS)" is a component of the "Coir Vikas Yojana". The scheme was launched by the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India for providing modern infrastructure facilities to the production units resulting in improvement of productivity and quality.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: What is the objective of this scheme?
Answer: The objectives of this component are:
To provide modern infrastructure facilities to the production units resulting in improvement of productivity and quality.
To support the establishment of new 'State-of-the-Art' Coir Processing Units. To spread the industry to potential areas.
To promote enhanced utilization of available raw materials.
To create more employment opportunities, especially for women in rural areas. To attract new generation entrepreneurs to the industry.
To modernize the existing coir units.
To promote the development and installation of information technology including Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP).

To support the production of high-value customer-oriented products. To make the Coir Industry integrated and competitive with modern technologies.
To facilitate the adoption of eco-friendly production techniques.
To achieve the target of a pollution-free coir industry with technological advancements.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
Answer: Coir Board, Kochi

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: Who are eligible for the assistance under the scheme CITUS?
Answer: Assistance will be available to entrepreneurs in the categories of individuals/partnership firms, SHGs, Associations, enterprises from small scale / medium / co-operative/ private sector / public sector, interested for production of value added coir /coir blended items, where coir is the dominant fiber by setting up new coir unit or upgrading the existing unit.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: Is it necessary for Coir Unit to register with the Coir Board?
Answer: Yes, all coir production/processing units registered with the Coir Board under Coir Industry (Registration) Rules, 2008, and having Udyog Aadhaar are eligible to apply for financial assistance for modernization under this scheme.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: What is the nature of assistance which is provided under scheme?
Answer: The financial assistance shall be 25% of the cost of admissible items of Plant and Machinery procured by the Coir units. The upper ceiling of the financial assistance will be [?]2.50 crore per coir unit/project.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: What is the purpose of providing financial assistance?
Answer: All eligible Coir units under the component will be entitled to get financial assistance for the procurement of eligible Plants and Machinery for modernization, upgradation, and/or establishing a new unit on making an application in the prescribed format for the purpose.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: How the financial assistance will be paid under the scheme?
Answer: The financial assistance will be payable only in Indian Rupees in India through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode and Public Finance Management System (PFMS) as reimbursement of the amount invested.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
Question: Which types of entrepreneurs are not eligible for assistance?
Answer: The financial assistance under this component will be available to entrepreneurs who have not availed of any Central Government subsidy under PMEGP, CUY, DPI, TUF, etc. for the same purpose.

Scheme: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
