Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: How often do I have to report back my progress after receiving seed fund?
Answer: 1. Each Incubator shall provide information on progress of selected startups (see Para 10 of guidelines) real-time to Startup India through their online dashboards and shall present the same to EAC on a quarterly basis
2. Incubator shall also report return on investment for each Startup.
3. Each incubator shall report the funds sanctioned, received, and disbursed to each startup for each financial year
4. Incubators would also submit detailed report on status of utilization of funds and audited expenditure for each financial year

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: I want to quit the scheme. What are the provisions?
Answer: An incubator can quit the scheme. The procedure for the same depends on the stage of the incubator in the application process.
1. If the incubator has been selected and the first tranche is approved, they will be required to write a short letter mentioning the reason to pull out of the process. Post the acknowledgment of the letter, they will find a cancel application button on the application tracker tab of their dashboard which will allow them to cancel their application

2. If the incubator has already received the first tranche, it will be required to write a short letter mentioning the reason to pull out of the process. Post acknowledgment of the letter, they will be obliged to return the fund along with the interest accumulated within 15 days. Post the acknowledgment of refund, they will find a cancel application butt

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: What is the process for selecting startups for seed fund?
Answer: 1. An online call for applications shall be hosted for startups on an ongoing basis on the Startup India portal
2. Applicants can apply for seed fund to any three incubators selected as disbursing partners for this scheme in order of their preference
3. All applications received will be shared online with respective incubators for further evaluation
4. The incubators shall shortlist applicants as per eligibility criteria
5. Incubator may shortlist applicants based on their evaluation for a presentation before ISMC

5. Incubator may shortlist applicants based on their evaluation for a presentation before ISMC
6. ISMC shall evaluate applicants based on their submissions and presentations and select startups for Seed Fund within 45 days of receipt of application
7. All incubators shall provide information about progress of evaluation of startups real-time to Startup India portal
8. Selected startups shall receive seed funding under the respective incubator that selects them as beneficiaries as per their preference shared during application
9. Incubator shall conduct due diligence of the startups and sign legal agreement with them
10. For grants, the first installment to any selected startup shall be released not more than 60 days from receipt of application from the startup.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: Do incubators need the approval of EAC for selecting or funding a startup?
Answer: No. The ISMC of each incubator will be responsible for evaluating and selecting startups for seed support under the scheme.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: What are the terms and conditions of seed funding through convertible debentures or debt or debt-linked instruments?
Answer: For startups being supported through convertible debentures, or debt, or debt-linked instruments, funds shall be provided at a rate of interest of not more than prevailing repo rate. The tenure should be fixed at the time of sanctioning the loan by the incubator, which shall be not more than 60 months (5 years). A moratorium of up to 12 months may be provided for the startups. Because of the early stage of the startups, this shall be unsecured and no guarantee from promoter or third-party will be required.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: How much seed funding can a startup receive under the scheme?
Answer: Seed Fund to an eligible startup by the incubator shall be disbursed as follows:
1. Up to [?] 20 Lakhs as grant for validation of Proof of Concept, or prototype development, or product trials. The grant shall be disbursed in milestone-based installments. These milestones can be related to development of prototype, product testing, building a product ready for market launch, etc.
2. Up to[?] 50 Lakhs of investment for market entry, commercialization, or scaling up through convertible debentures or debt or debt-linked instruments.
3. Not more than 20% of the total grant to an incubator shall be given as grants to startups by incubator.
4. A startup applicant can avail seed support in the form of grant and debt/convertible debentures each once as per the guidelines of the scheme.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: If the startup requires legal help for finalizing their seed fund engagement with an incubator, who will bear the cost for these services?
Answer: The startup shall bear the cost of any consultant hired to guide them finalizing their seed fund engagement with an incubator.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: Who will be bearing the cost for due diligence of the startups?
Answer: The Management Fee provisioned to each selected incubator will be utilized for administrative expenditure, selection and due diligence of startups, and monitoring of progress of beneficiary startups.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: Do incubators need to sign an Agreement with selected startups?
Answer: The incubator shall execute a legal agreement with the selected startups before the release of the first installment. The incubators shall ensure that the necessary terms and conditions, including milestones, related to the Seed Fund are clearly detailed in the agreement.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: Will incubators be provided a sample Agreement to sign with each selected startup?
Answer: Yes. The incubator can make suitable changes to the sample agreement on the basis of the terms and conditions finalized with each selected startup. However, no mandatory clause of the Guidelines may be changed in this Agreement.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: Can incubators charge any fee from the selected startups?
Answer: A startup selected by an incubator for assistance under this scheme shall not be charged any fees. The incubator or any of its staff members shall not charge any fee in cash or in kind from applicants or beneficiaries under the scheme for any process of selection, disbursement, incubation, or monitoring.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: How often do incubators have to interact with selected startups?
Answer: Each startup will be required to touch base with the incubator team and share updates with them at least once in 15 days via videoconferences or physical meetings. These updates should be shared on the scheme dashboard at least on a monthly basis.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: What parameters does an incubator need to track for selected startups?
Answer: The following shall be tracked and recorded by incubators for all beneficiary startups:
1. Progress of proof of concept
2. Progress of prototype development
3. Progress of product development
4. Progress of field trials
5. Progress of market launch
6. Quantum of loan, angel or VC funding raised
7. Jobs created by startup
8. Turnover of startup
9. Any other appropriate parameter

7. Jobs created by startup
8. Turnover of startup
9. Any other appropriate parameter
Selected startups shall furnish details on above parameters to incubator in all progress reports. The incubator shall provide the above information real-time to Startup India through their online dashboards and shall present the same to EAC on a quarterly basis. Incubator shall also report return on investment for each Startup.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: When can incubators ask DPIIT for the next installment of funds?
Answer: When the cash-in-hand of the incubator goes below 10% of the total commitment by EAC, the Incubator may request for the next installment, which shall be released to incubator within 30 days of submission of proof of achievement of milestones.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: We have received a tranche of funds but have not been able to select many startups. What happens to the unutilized funds?
Answer: Rate of interest (as defined under GFR) on unutilized funds available with incubator shall be taken into account and adjusted at the time of next release. If the Incubator has not utilized at least 50% of the total commitment within the first 2 years, then the Incubator will not be eligible for any further drawdowns. It will return all unutilized funds along with interest. In case of poor performance of any selected incubator, EAC may decide to discontinue seed fund support to the incubator and take further action as may be required.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: How does an incubator utilize net returns from seed funding into startups?
Answer: Any net return received from beneficiary startup can be used for further funding in startups as per guidelines of this scheme (net returns shall include principal, interest, and profits). In case of no further funding of startups using this money for three years, this shall be returned to DPIIT.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: What happens if a startup fails?
Answer: It is understood that every startup cannot be successful.

Scheme: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Incubators
Question: Can an incubator reapply to the scheme if they successfully disburse funds sanctioned to them?
Answer: An incubator can reapply for funds under the Scheme when it has disbursed or committed its entire previously released grant.

- Technical textiles

Scheme: Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Support for Group Nurseries
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
**Step 1: Initiation by the Extension Officer**
The Extension Officers of the Coffee Board will motivate a group of tribal growers in each of the localities/villages to raise a coffee nursery on a community basis. This caters to the requirement of seedlings for annual expansion and consolidation programs.
**Step 2: Location and Seedling Selection**
The groups themselves decide on the nursery's location and the number of seedlings to be raised. This decision is made in consultation with the Extension Officer of the Coffee Board, considering factors like water availability and other essential resources required for a healthy nursery.

**Step 3: Group Responsibilities**
The group takes the responsibility of motivating their members to participate in raising the nursery and distributing the seedlings among the members.
**Step 4: Cost Estimation and Control**
The concerned Extension Officer estimates the cost involved in raising the group nurseries. It is ensured that the cost of raising each healthy coffee seedling does not exceed ₹5, inclusive of input and labor costs.
**Step 5: Proposal Submission and Consolidation**
The Extension Officer submits a proposal containing details of the number of seedlings to be raised and the associated expenditure to the Deputy Director (E). The Deputy Director consolidates the requirements for his region and submits them to the Joint Director (E) in Guwahati, along with recommendations.

**Step 6: Regional Consolidation and Recommendations**
The Joint Director (E) consolidates the overall requirements for the North Eastern Region (NER) and submits the proposal, along with recommendations, to the Director of Research.
**Step 7: Scrutiny and Sanction**
The Director of Research scrutinizes the proposal and submits it to the Head Office in Bengaluru, along with recommendations for sanction.
**Step 8: Phased Funding Release**
After sanction, the concerned Joint Director (Extn.) or Deputy Director (E) releases the approved amount in a phased manner at different stages of raising the nurseries.

Further, such a cluster will have 200 to 2042 beneficiaries (spinners, weavers, stitches, and other skilled artisans). Each spinner will be given two charkhas of 10 spindles each. On average, it is considered that such a cluster will have about 1000 charkhas.

* To boost the rural economy and help in arresting migration from rural to urban areas.
* To leverage low-cost, innovative technologies and processes for sustenance.

Scheme: Design Scheme Under MSME Innovative Scheme
Question: What is the objectives of Design Scheme?
Answer: The objective of this component is to bring Indian manufacturing sector and Design expertise/ Design fraternity on to a common platform. It aims to provide expert advice and cost-effective solution on real time design problems for new product development, its continuous improvement and value addition in existing/new products.

Scheme: Design Scheme Under MSME Innovative Scheme
Question: What are the broad activities of MSME Innovative scheme?
Answer: The Design scheme is divided in two major parts, viz., Design Projects and Design Awareness Programme.
a. Design Project - To facilitate MSMEs to develop new design strategies and or design related products through interventions and consultancy. 
b. Design Awareness Programme: The objective is to create general awareness and sensitization about the value and power of design for businesses through seminars, talks, workshops etc. The purpose of these activities is to sensitize MSMEs about the usage of design/innovation in various facets of their industry.

Scheme: Design Scheme Under MSME Innovative Scheme
Question: What type of financial assistance provided under the scheme?
Answer: Two types of financial assistance provided under the scheme: Design Project and Student Project.

Scheme: Design Scheme Under MSME Innovative Scheme

definition in MSMED and should have a valid UAM or Udyam Registration. The manufacturing MSMEs may be a profitable entity preferably in the last 1 year of its operations.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme

Answer: DDRS stands for Deendayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme under which, the Central Government has been providing grant-in-aid to non-governmental organizations (NGOs) for projects relating to rehabilitation of persons with disabilities aimed at enabling them to reach and maintain their optimal, physical, sensory, intellectual, physic- social functional levels.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme
Question: What is/are the Objectives of DDRS?
Answer: 1. To create an enabling environment to ensure equal opportunities, equity, social justice and empowerment of persons with disabilities.
2. To encourage voluntary action for ensuring effective implementation of the Revised Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (RPwD Act, 2016).

Scheme: Deen Dayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme
Question: What are the activities/components admissible for grant under DDRS?
Answer: I. Recurring expenditure
II. Non-recurring expenditure such as furniture, equipment, books etc.

Scheme: Deen Dayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme
Question: What are the model projects under the DDRS?
Answer: 1. Pre-School, Early Intervention and Training.
2. Special Schools.
3. Project for Cerebral Palsied Children
4. Project for Rehabilitation of Leprosy Cured Persons
5. Half Way Home for Psycho-Social Rehabilitation of Treated and Controlled people with mental Illness
6. Home Based Rehabilitation Programme/Home Management Programme
7. Project for Community Based Rehabilitation.
8. Project for Low Vision Centers
9. Projects for Human Resource Development.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is Maximum Project Cost Allowed Under PMEGP?
Answer: Rs.25.00 lakhs for the manufacturing unit and Rs.10.00 lakhs for Service Unit

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is The Component Of Project Cost?
Answer: Capital Expenditure Loan, one cycle of working capital and 10% of project cost as own contribution in case of General category and 5% of project cost in case of weaker section.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Which Are The Financial Agencies?
Answer: 27 Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks(RRB), Co-operative Banks, and Private Scheduled Commercial Banks approved by respective State Task Force Committee.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: How The Capital Expenditure Loan / Cash Credit Limit Be Utilized ?
Answer: Working Capital at least once should touch the 100% limit of Cash Credit within three years of the Lock-in period of M.M. and not less than 75% of the utilization of the sanctioned limit on average.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Where The Beneficiary Has To Submit His/Her Application/ Project?
Answer: The beneficiary can submit his/her application/Project online on kvic website www.kvic.org.in / kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal. A list of office addresses of KVIC/KVIB/DIC is available at our website.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is Village Industry ?
Answer: Any Village Industry (except those mentioned in the negative list) located in the Rural Area which produces any goods or renders any service with or without the use of power and in which the fixed capital investment for head of a full time artisans or worker does not exceed Rs.1.00 lakh in plain area and Rs.1.50 lakhs in hilly areas and for A & N Island and Laxdeep Rs.4.5 Lakhs.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is Rural Area ?
Answer: Any area classified as Village as per the revenue record of the State, irrespective of the population. It also includes an area even if classified as town provided its population does not exceed 20000.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is Age Limit ?
Answer: Any adult beneficiary above 18 years is eligible for financing under PMEGP.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Are The Main Criteria Of Project?
Answer: It should fulfill the criteria of rural area (for Rural Area project), per capita investment, own contribution, negative list, and the unit should be a new one

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Whether EDP Training Is Compulsory?
Answer: Before MM Claim through the PMEGP portal, EDP training of 10 working days for a Project cost of More than 5.00 lakhs and 6 Working days of training for up to Project Cost of 5.00 lakhs to the beneficiary is compulsory

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Whether Collateral Security Is Mandatory?
Answer: As per RBI guidelines, the project costing up to Rs.10.00 lakhs under PMEGP loans are free from collateral security. The CGTSME provided a collateral guarantee for the project beyond Rs.5.00 lakhs and up to Rs.25.00 lakhs under the PMEGP scheme.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is PMEGP Scheme, And What Are Its Objectives?
Answer: Answer: PMEGP stands for Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme, which is a credit-linked subsidy scheme launched by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, to generate employment opportunities in the country. The main objective of the scheme is to create self-employment opportunities for unemployed youth and women entrepreneurs in rural and urban areas.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Who Is Eligible To Apply For PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Age Limit For The Applicants?
Answer: Answer: Any individual above 18 years of age can apply for the PMEGP scheme. However, the maximum age limit for applying is 35 years for general category applicants and 40 years for SC/ST/OBC/PH/Women candidates.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: How Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Application Procedure?
Answer: Answer: You can apply for the PMEGP scheme through the online portal of KVIC, or offline by submitting the application form to the nearest KVIC office or bank. The application procedure involves filling up the application form, attaching the necessary documents, and submitting it along with the project report.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Are The Different Types Of Projects That Can Be Set Up Under The PMEGP Scheme?
Answer: Answer: The PMEGP scheme supports various types of projects, including manufacturing, service, and business projects. The projects should be viable and have the potential to generate employment opportunities.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: How Much Financial Assistance Can I Expect To Receive Under The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Repayment Period?
Answer: Answer: Under the PMEGP scheme, financial assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy, which ranges from 15% to 35% of the project cost, depending on the category of the applicant. The remaining amount can be obtained as a bank loan. The repayment period for the loan is generally 3 to 7 years.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Can I Apply For Multiple Projects Under The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Maximum Limit?
Answer: Answer: No, an individual can apply for only one project under the PMEGP scheme. However, a group of individuals can apply for a group project, subject to a maximum of 10 members.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Are The Documents Required To Apply For The PMEGP Scheme?
Answer: Answer: The documents required for PMEGP scheme application include a project report, proof of identity and address, caste certificate (if applicable), educational qualification certificate, and bank account details.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: How Long Does It Take For The PMEGP Scheme Application To Be Processed?
Answer: Answer: The processing time for the PMEGP scheme application varies from state to state and depends on various factors such as the completeness of the application, the availability of funds, and the number of applications received.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme For An Existing Business?
Answer: Answer: No, the PMEGP scheme is meant for setting up a new business or for expanding an existing business. An existing business is not eligible for financial assistance under the PMEGP scheme.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is The Role Of The Khadi And Village Industries Commission (KVIC) In The PMEGP Scheme?
Answer: Answer: KVIC is the nodal agency for implementing the PMEGP scheme. It is responsible for receiving and processing the applications, conducting training programs, and disbursing the subsidy to the beneficiaries through the banks.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Is The Project Report, And How Do I Prepare It?
Answer: Answer: The project report is a detailed document that provides information about the proposed project, its feasibility, and financial viability. It includes details like project cost, sources of funding, marketing plan, and expected income and expenses. KVIC provides a format for preparing the project report, which can be downloaded from their website.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme Offline?
Answer: Answer: Yes, you can apply for the PMEGP scheme offline by submitting the application form along with the project report and necessary documents to the nearest KVIC office or bank.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme Online?
Answer: Answer: Yes, you can apply for the PMEGP scheme online through the KVIC portal. The process involves registering on the portal, filling up the application form, and uploading the necessary documents.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: What Are The Documents Required For The PMEGP Scheme Application?
Answer: Answer: The documents required for the PMEGP scheme application include proof of identity and address, educational qualification certificate, caste certificate (if applicable), project report, and bank account details.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: Can I Make Changes To My PMEGP Scheme Application After Submission?
Answer: Answer: No, you cannot make changes to your PMEGP scheme application after submission. Therefore, it is important to ensure that all the information provided in the application is accurate and complete before submitting it.

Scheme: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
Question: How Long Does It Take For The PMEGP Scheme Application To Be Processed?

Answer: Answer: Once your PMEGP scheme application is approved, you will receive an approval letter from KVIC or the bank, along with the sanction letter stating the amount of subsidy and loan that you are eligible for.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
**Step 1:** The State or Union Territory identifies Government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for upgradation and prepares the Request for Proposal (RFP) along with defined eligibility criteria.
**Step 2:** The State or Union Territory issues the RFP to invite proposals from eligible Anchor Industry Partners (AIP) or industry partners.
**Step 3:** The applicant submits the proposal along with the Strategic Investment Plan (SIP), including details of infrastructure, courses, human resources, financials, and implementation strategy.

**Step 4:** The submitted proposals are evaluated through pre-qualification, technical assessment of the SIP, and financial evaluation.
**Step 5:** The State Government selects suitable proposals and forwards them to the National Steering Committee (NSC) for final approval.
**Step 6:** Upon approval, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) is formed for each cluster, and agreements such as the Shareholder Agreement (SHA) and License Agreement (LA) are executed.
**Step 7:** An escrow account is established for the SPV, and contributions from the Central Government, State Government, and Industry are deposited into it.

**Step 8:** The SPV prepares the Annual Operational Plan (AOP) aligned with the approved [Strategic Investment Plan (SIP)](https://www.msde.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/04/407d256a1244bfbcce7cf324f216fc1f.pdf).
**Step 9:** Funds are released in stages, starting with an initial advance and followed by instalments based on utilisation, performance, and approval of the AOP.
**Step 10:** The SPV undertakes the implementation of ITI upgradation, including infrastructure development, course delivery, and provision of training and student services.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: What is PM SETU and what is its objective?
Answer: PM SETU stands for Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) to upgrade 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) as aspirational skilling institutions and establish 5 National Centres of Excellence, aligned with the goal of "Viksit Bharat" by 2047.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: What is the total outlay of the scheme and how is it shared?
Answer: The total outlay is ₹60,000 crore over five years, shared as:

- Central Government: ₹30,000 crore (50%)
- State Governments: ₹20,000 crore (33%)
- Industry: ₹10,000 crore (17%)

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: Who can become an Anchor Industry Partner (AIP)?
Answer: Eligible entities include:

- Industry partners (credible companies/manufacturers with Indian operations, including PSUs)
- Industry associations or consortia
- Industry-led foundations (CSR/philanthropy arms of corporates)
- Academic institutions promoted/operated by industry (e.g., corporate universities, sectoral skilling institutions)

Entities debarred by any government agency are not eligible.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: What is the Hub-and-Spoke model under PM SETU?
Answer: Under this model, 1,000 Government ITIs will be upgraded in clusters, with 200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs. Each Hub ITI will have, on average, 4 associated Spoke ITIs, all equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure, machinery, and equipment. Mini-Hubs are allowed for the North-Eastern and Hilly regions.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: What is the shareholding structure of the Industry-led SPV?
Answer: The Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) is incorporated as a Section 8 Company with shareholding:

- Anchor Industry Partner (AIP): 51%
- Central Government: 24.5%
- State Government: 24.5%

The SPV has an initial share capital of ₹1,00,000 with each shareholder contributing pro rata.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: What is the maximum funding per ITI?
Answer: - Hub ITI: Outlay not exceeding ₹81 crore over 5 years (Central: ₹40 crore, State: ₹30 crore, Industry: ₹11 crore).
- Spoke ITI: Outlay not exceeding ₹40 crore over 5 years (Central: ₹18 crore, State: ₹17 crore, Industry: ₹5 crore).
- One Hub + Four Spokes cluster total: ₹241 crore.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: How are funds disbursed under the scheme?
Answer: - Year 1: Initial advance of up to 10% of total project outlay upon SIP approval
- Years 2-5: Annual instalments released in two tranches of 50% each
- First instalment requires at least 75% utilization of previous funds, AOP approval, and 80% KPI achievement
- Second instalment requires 50% mid-year KPI achievement and full industry/state contribution
- All transactions through escrow account at a Scheduled Commercial Bank; no cash transactions allowed.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: What is the application process for industries to become AIP?
Answer: Step 1: State/UT releases Expression of Interest (EOI) within 30 days of guidelines issuance
Step 2: State/UT floats Request for Proposal (RFP) within 45 days
Step 3: AIP submits Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) within 75 days
Step 4: SSC recommends SIP within 90 days
Step 5: NSC approves SIP within 100 days
Step 6: SPV (Section 8 Company) is formed within 120 days
Step 7: Shareholders' Agreement (SHA) and License Agreement (LA) are signed.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: How many new courses will be introduced and what is the curriculum structure?
Answer: - Hub ITIs: Average of 4 new courses and upgradation of 10 existing courses
- Spoke ITIs: Average of 2 new courses and upgradation of 8 existing courses
- Modular structure: 240 hours per module (8 credits each), with 3 Core Modules (720 hours) common across all ITIs and Specific Modules customized as per industry needs
- Total: 1,590 hours (1,200 + 150 OJT + 240 optional) earning 53 credits
- New courses approved through green channel within 15 working days.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM‑SETU) : Component I 
Question: What are the special provisions for North-Eastern and Hilly States?
Answer: - Funding pattern for NE and Hilly States: Centre:State:Industry ratio is 74.7%:8.3%:17% (with central funding including operational costs)
- For Union Territories without legislature: 83%:0%:17% (no UT share)
- Mini-Hubs allowed with relaxed definition of Hubs and Spokes for these regions
- Indicative cluster allocation: NE States - 10 clusters, Hill States and UTs - 10 clusters.

Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0- Special Projects
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
**Stage 1:** The applicant first registers on the [Skill India Digital (SID)](https://www.skillindiadigital.gov.in/home) platform or the mobile application developed for the purpose; profile verification is completed through mobile-based OTP / eKYC, and a de-duplication check is carried out.
**Stage 2:** The applicant is counselled by the PIA/trainer on areas including a brief about MSDE, the Skill India programme, and RPL processes; eligibility for RPL certification; benefits and how to avail them; possible career progression (vertical and horizontal); and employment opportunities. The Induction Video on RPL is also shown at this stage.

**Stage 3:** A de-duplication check is carried out against the data available in the Skill India Digital database, so that the applicant is not enrolled again in the same job role in which he/she was trained earlier.
**Stage 4:** The applicant's profile is completed, with existing details fetched from other portals such as e-Shram and National Career Services (NCS).
**Stage 5:** The applicant avails online counselling offered through Skill India Digital to select an appropriate course and Training Centre.
**Stage 6:** The applicant selects the nearest Training Centre based on the availability of the preferred job role and the quality of training infrastructure (rating, centre profile), or is mapped automatically through logic-based mapping to the nearest Training Centre.

**Stage 7:** On selection and enrolment, the applicant undergoes training, followed by On-the-Job Training (OJT) in applicable job roles.
**Stage 8:** The applicant appears for assessment by an NCVET-approved Awarding Body / Assessment Agency after completion of On-the-Job Training, requiring more than 70% biometric attendance to be eligible.
**Stage 9:** On successful completion, the applicant is awarded a Quick Response (QR) code-based digital certificate, issued via DigiLocker, an email/phone download link, and the Skill India Digital profile page, along with one printed certificate provided free of cost by the Training Provider.

**Step 1:** Determine the Category 1 for a population of 15,00,000 or more with a minimum of 7.0 acres; Category 2 for a population between 5,00,000 and 15,00,000 with a minimum of 5.0 acres (2.5 to 3.0 acres for the North East region, hilly terrains and island territories); Category 3 for a population less than 5,00,000 with a minimum of 2.0 acres.

**Step 4:** Obtain the Detailed Project Report format at [Annexure E](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), with [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) for the Physical Report on Site.

**Step 9:** The Detailed Project Report is appraised by the Project Appraisal Committee for recommendation to the competent authority.
**Step 10:** Obtain approval from the Government of India.

**Step 10:** Obtain approval from the Government of India.
**Step 11:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding with the National Council of Science Museums, if implemented by it.
**Step 12:** Form the Society immediately after approval of the project and release of the State/Union Territory share of capital cost and corpus fund; the corpus fund share is released upfront prior to commencement of works.

Where land is located in the heart of the city, and availability is scarce, the land requirement may be relaxed for science centres, with the building constructed in multiple stories utilising the available Floor Space Ratio; however, the Science Park shall be an integral part of the science centre.

Scheme: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Science Centre (Category-I, Category-II, Category-III)
Question: What is the funding pattern?

Answer: Under Type A, the Ministry of Culture may consider providing full funding through the National Council of Science Museums for Science Centres in locations or regions where Science Centre activities have not yet started, or in priority areas; in no case will more than one Science Centre be set up in any State or Union Territory in future under the scheme, and this provision is not applicable where National Council of Science Museums centres already exist. Under Type B, the capital cost is shared 50:50, except for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim where it is 90:10, and the corpus fund is shared 20:80. Under Type C, the State Government/Union Territory fully funds the project with technical support from the National Council of Science Museums against payment of consultancy

Scheme: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Science Centre (Category-I, Category-II, Category-III)
Question: How is the money released, and how much must the State pay upfront?

Question: How is the money released, and how much must the State pay upfront?
Answer: The capital expenditure is released at 40 per cent in the first year, 40 per cent in the second year and 20 per cent in the third year for Category 1 and Category 2, and at 60 per cent in the first year and 40 per cent in the second year for Category 3. The corpus fund share is released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of works. The upfront release by the State/Union Territory Government is ₹23.35 crore, ₹12.82 crore or ₹27.94 crore for Category 1; ₹12.67 crore, ₹7.01 crore or ₹15.21 crore for Category 2; and ₹3.79 crore, ₹2.09 crore or ₹4.53 crore for Category 3, depending on location.

Under Type C, the State Government/Union Territory shall do the construction of the building as per inputs from the National Council of Science Museums and develop the Science Park as per its advice, with the National Council of Science Museums providing technical and professional support at cost and consultancy charges.

Steps:

**Step 05**: Submit the application form with an initial amount of investment/deposit.
**Step 06:** Upon processing your application, a KVP certificate is issued immediately. Keep the documents safe which will need at the time of maturity.
> **Procedure for payment:**

Payment for the purchase of a Certificate may be made to a Post Office or Bank in any of the following modes, namely:

 - by cash; or
 - by locally executed cheque, pay order, or demand draft drawn in favour of the Post Master; or
 - by presenting a duly signed withdrawal form or cheque together with the passbook for withdrawal from a Savings Account standing in a credit of the purchaser at the same Post Office or Bank.

> **Issue of Certificates:**

- On payment being made, except where payment is made by a cheque, pay order, or demand draft, a Certificate shall be issued immediately and the date of such Certificate shall be the date of payment.
 - Where payment for the purchase of a Certificate is made by cheque, pay order, or demand draft, the Certificate shall not be issued before the proceeds of the cheque, pay order, or demand draft, as the case may be, are realized and the date of such Certificate shall be the date of encashment of the cheque, pay order or demand draft, as the case may be.

- If, for any reason a Certificate cannot be issued immediately, a provisional receipt shall be given to the purchaser which may later be exchanged for a Certificate, and in such a case the date of the Certificate shall be the date of provisional receipt.
> **Premature closure of account:**

3. Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-paragraph (2) of the scheme guideline, if an account is closed any time after the expiry of two years and six months from the date of opening of the account, the amount, inclusive of interest shall be payable as per specified rate. 
> **Transfer of account:**

- In the event of the death of the depositor of a single account or of all the depositors in a joint account, the deposit shall be payable to the nominee if a nomination exists or to the legal heir(s).
 - Where there are not more than three surviving nominees or legal heirs, they may, at their option continue the account and receive the amount of deposit along with interest on maturity in the manner provided for in this scheme, as if they had opened the account themselves.
 - Where the account is not continued under sub-paragraph (2) of the scheme guideline, it shall be closed and the amount of deposit along with interest as provided in paragraph 6 shall be repaid.

- On the death of one or two of the account holders in a joint account, the surviving account holder or holders, if any, shall be treated as the owner or owners of the account and such account holder or holders may continue the account under sub-paragraph (2) of the scheme guideline or close the account under sub-paragraph (3) of the scheme guideline.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: What is the main objective of the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana"?
Answer: The main objective of the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" is to provide financial assistance of ₹5,000 to support women during maternity, compensate partial wage loss, and encourage proper healthcare practices among pregnant and lactating mothers, especially after the birth of their second child.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: Who is eligible to receive benefits under the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana"?
Answer: Women who belong to specific eligible categories such as Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, persons with disabilities (40% or more), Below Poverty Line (BPL) cardholders, beneficiaries of PMJAY under Ayushman Bharat, E-shram cardholders, women farmers under the Kisan Samman Nidhi, MGNREGA job cardholders, and those with an annual family income below ₹8,00,000 are eligible to receive benefits under the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana".

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: What are the conditions that must be met to receive the ₹5,000 benefit under this scheme?
Answer: To receive the ₹5,000/- benefit under the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana", the applicant must register her pregnancy, undergo at least one antenatal check-up within six months from the Last Menstrual Period (LMP), ensure the birth of the child is officially registered, and confirm that the newborn has received the first cycle of immunizations including BCG, OPV, DPT, and Hepatitis-B.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: Is the benefit amount under this scheme disbursed in multiple instalments or as a single payment?
Answer: The benefit amount under the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" is disbursed as a single payment of ₹5,000, provided all specified conditions and eligibility criteria are fulfilled by the applicant.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: Can the scheme be availed for the birth of the first child?
Answer: No, the scheme specifically provides financial benefits only for the birth of a second child who is a boy, and it does not cover the first child or girl children under its current guidelines.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: Who is responsible for implementing the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana"?
Answer: The "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" is implemented by the Women and Child Development Department, Government of Haryana, which ensures the proper execution of the scheme through Anganwadi Centres and approved health facilities.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: Are pregnant women working as Anganwadi Workers, Anganwadi Helpers, or ASHAs eligible for this scheme?
Answer: Yes, pregnant and lactating women who are employed as Anganwadi Workers (AWWs), Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs), or Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) are eligible to receive benefits under the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" if they meet the other eligibility requirements.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: How is the financial benefit provided to the beneficiaries under this scheme?
Answer: The financial benefit under the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" is transferred directly to the bank account of the eligible beneficiary through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism after verification of all required documents and fulfilment of scheme conditions.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: Can a woman avail the scheme more than once for different children?
Answer: No, a woman can avail the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" only once for the birth of her second child who is a boy, and it cannot be availed for any other births or subsequent children.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: From which date are children born eligible under this scheme?
Answer: Children born on or after 8th March 2022 are eligible for benefits under the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana", provided all other conditions and eligibility criteria are fulfilled.

Scheme: Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana
Question: What is the role of Anganwadi Centres in the implementation of this scheme?
Answer: Anganwadi Centres play a vital role in the implementation of the "Mukhya Mantri Matritva Sahayata Yojana" as they facilitate pregnancy registration, provide antenatal services, assist in documentation, and coordinate with health facilities to ensure scheme benefits are delivered to eligible women.

Answer: The applicants may visit the [Antyodaya-SARAL Portal](https://saralharyana.gov.in/) to apply for the scheme.

Question: What is the main objective of the "Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for Translation of Scholarly Works"?
Answer: The primary objective of the "Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for Translation of Scholarly Works" is to encourage literary and cultural exchange by supporting the translation of high-quality literary, research, and scholarly works between Gujarati and other Indian languages.

Scheme: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for Translation of Scholarly Works
Question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
Answer: Any individual translator or eligible institution that wishes to translate a scholarly or literary work from another Indian language into Gujarati, or from Gujarati into another Indian language, can apply under the "Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for Translation of Scholarly Works", provided they meet all the eligibility criteria.

Scheme: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for Translation of Scholarly Works
Question: What types of works are considered scholarly or literary under the scheme?
Answer: Under this scheme, scholarly or literary works include original novels, plays, essays, short stories, poetry, literary criticism, one-act plays, cultural essays, and research-oriented manuscripts that contribute to the promotion of knowledge and literature.

Scheme: Loan based Scheme for Pay and Use Community Toilets
Section: Application Process
Mode: Online
Steps:
1. Loan applications are submitted by the applicants to the district offices of SCAs of NSKFDC of RRBs and Nationalised Banks.
 1. These applications are then sent to the head offices where the project proposal is appraised by SCA/RRBs/Nationalised Banks and the projects are sent back to NSKFDC along with recommendations.
 1. The Project Appraisal Committee of NSKFDC then appraises the proposals and after finding them in order places it in front of their board of directors for their approval.
 1. Once the board of directors approves the project, the letter of sanction is issued by SCAs/ RRBs/Nationalised Banks.

1. Once all the terms and conditions have been accepted, the necessary documents and funds are then released to the concerned beneficiaries.
 1. NSKFDC released the funds with the receipt of demand being made from the SCAs/ RRBs/Nationalised Banks after taking into consideration all the parameters of release as per the Lending Policies & Guidelines (LPG) of NSKFDC.

Scheme: Khadya Suraksha Yojana
Section: Application Process
Mode: Offline
Steps:
**Step-1:** The applicant need to Downloads the [document](https://jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in//Content/UploadFolder/Scheme/FOOD/NFSA/DOC_203_2cf8164c-98b5-43a0-958e-fdecd2ee7a68.pdf) and get the application form from page no. 4.
**Step-2:** Carefully read any instructions or guidelines provided. 
**Step-3:** Collect all the information and documents.
 - Ration Card.
 - Aadhaar Card.
 - Bhamashah Card.
 - Cast Certificate
 - BPL Card (If applicable).
 - Affidavit (available in form page no. 6).
**Step-5:** Make a copy of the completed form for your records before submitting it. This will serve as a reference in case you need to refer back to the information provided.

**Step-6:** Submit the form to the concerned Appellate Officer (Sub Division/District Logistics Officer) .
**Step-7:** The Appellate Officer will thoroughly scrutinize the application. If complete and correct, the applicant's name will be added to the food security list. However, if doubts arise regarding the presented documents, the officer will only proceed after clarification.
**Step-8:** The Appellate Officer will issue an appeal order with a computer-generated digitized signature, automatically updating the applicant's name in the online food security list.

**Step-9:** The responsibility of the Appellate Officers is limited to verifying the completeness of the application and attached certificates. If any applicant is found to have provided false information to gain inclusion in the food security list, their name will be canceled, and legal action will be taken.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: What is the "Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana" and who is it meant for?
Answer: The "Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana" is a financial assistance scheme launched by the Social Justice and Empowerment Department, Government of Haryana, which is meant for permanent residents of Haryana who suffer accidental death or permanent disability and are not enrolled under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: What benefits are provided under the "Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana"?
Answer: Under the "Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana", a one-time financial assistance of ₹1,00,000 is provided in the event of accidental death or in cases of permanent disability involving the total loss of eyes, hands, or feet.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme in case of accidental death?
Answer: In case of accidental death, the eligible claimants under this scheme include the deceased person’s spouse (if not remarried), all unmarried children in equal share, followed by the deceased’s mother or father, and no other person outside of these relations is allowed to claim the benefit.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: What are the age criteria to apply for the scheme benefits?
Answer: To be eligible under the scheme, the applicant—whether deceased or disabled—must be between the ages of 18 and 70 years at the time of the accident.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: Can a person already enrolled under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) avail this scheme?
Answer: No, a person who has registered under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana by depositing the ₹12 premium before the date of the accident is not eligible to avail benefits under the "Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana".

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: What kind of accidents are considered valid under the scheme?
Answer: Only accidents that result in death or permanent and complete disability such as the total loss of both eyes, both limbs, or a combination of one eye and one limb are considered valid for benefit under this scheme.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: Can a disabled person file the claim personally under the scheme?
Answer: Yes, in case of permanent disability, the disabled person who suffered the accident is the sole and rightful claimant for receiving the assistance under the scheme.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: Is this scheme applicable to residents of Haryana who are temporarily living outside the state?
Answer: No, only those individuals who are both permanent residents of Haryana and are residing in Haryana at the time of the accident are eligible for benefits under this scheme.

Scheme: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana
Question: Can a remarried spouse claim the benefit if the original deceased partner was eligible?
Answer: No, a spouse who has remarried after the death of the eligible person is not allowed to claim the benefit under the "Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Durghtana Sahayta Yojana".

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: What is the objective of the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families"?
Answer: The primary objective of the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families" is to provide financial assistance of ₹20,000 to eligible low-income families in the state of Haryana who have lost their main earning member, thereby helping them cope with immediate financial distress caused by the death.

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: Who can apply for the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families"?
Answer: Any permanent resident of Haryana who is registered in the Below Poverty Line (BPL) list or identified as destitute and belongs to a family where the breadwinner has died, and no other source of income or government pension is available, can apply for the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families."

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: What is the age limit to apply under the scheme?
Answer: The applicant, as well as the deceased breadwinner, must fall within the age bracket of 18 to 59 years at the time of death in order to be considered eligible for the benefit under the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families."

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: What amount of financial support is provided under the scheme?
Answer: The scheme provides a one-time financial support of ₹20,000/- to the eligible surviving family member who is recognized as the head of the family following the death of the primary earning member.

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: Can both spouses receive benefits under this scheme?
Answer: Yes, under the provisions of the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families", both husband and wife are individually entitled to the financial assistance if they meet all the necessary eligibility conditions and have lost their respective spouse who was the main earner.

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: What is the deadline for applying under the scheme after the death of the breadwinner?
Answer: The application for the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families" must be submitted within one year from the date of the death of the breadwinner, beyond which the application will not be considered.

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: Who is considered the head of the family for receiving the benefit?
Answer: The benefit under the scheme is provided to the surviving family member who, after proper investigation and verification, is identified as the new head of the family, which may include the spouse, minor children, unmarried daughters, or dependent parents.

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: What defines a family under this scheme?
Answer: Under the "National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families", the family is defined to include the husband, wife, minor children, unmarried daughters, dependent parents, and in certain cases, even the parents of a woman if they are residing in her household with her and her husband.

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: Are there any exclusions specified in the scheme guidelines?
Answer: Yes, exclusions under the scheme include families where the children are Class-I or Class-II gazetted officers, professionals such as doctors, engineers, or chartered accountants, or if the deceased’s parents are income tax payees, or if any family member holds or has held public office as an MP, MLA, or chairman of a board or corporation.

Scheme: National Family Benefit Scheme for BPL Families
Question: What is the process for applying to the "National Family Benefits Scheme for BPL Families"?
Answer: The applicants may visit the [Antyodaya-SARAL Portal](https://saralharyana.gov.in/) to apply for the scheme.

Answer: To apply for the "National Family Benefits Scheme for BPL Families", the applicant may visit the nearest Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre).

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: If I belong to the General Category, how much subsidy am I eligible for?
Answer: As a General Category applicant, you are eligible for a 40% subsidy on the project cost.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: Being a woman applicant, what subsidy benefit can I get under this scheme?
Answer: As a woman applicant, you are eligible for a 60% subsidy on the project cost.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: Can I apply if I don’t have a Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP)?
Answer: No, having a valid Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP) is mandatory for applying.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: Will my leased land be accepted for this scheme?
Answer: Yes, if you have a registered lease deed for at least 10 years, your leased land will be accepted.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: I have a borewell on my land. Can I use it for this project?
Answer: Yes, water from borewells, open wells, canals, rivers, springs, etc., is acceptable for the project.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: Will the government take care of the maintenance after construction?
Answer: No, you will be responsible for operating, managing, and maintaining the unit after construction at your own cost.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: Do I need to include anything specific in the infrastructure setup?
Answer: Yes, your setup must include all essential requirements, especially water treatment units for RAS/Biofloc.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: Are there any service charges I should be aware of?
Answer: Yes, you need to pay ₹10/- to the Atal Seva Kendra and an additional ₹10/- as service charges.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: How long will it take for my application to be processed?
Answer: Your application will be processed within 50 days as per the Right to Service (RTS) timeline.

Scheme: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
Question: Do I have to prepare a project report while applying?
Answer: Yes, you need to submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR) or a Self-Contained Proposal (SCP) as per the guidelines.

Scheme: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme
Question: What is the full name of NCCS? Which department manages this organization?
Answer: The full name of NCCS is "National Centre for Communication Security". It is a subordinate office of Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India.

Scheme: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme
Question: What are the areas of activity of NCCS?
Answer: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) responsible for the implementation of ComSeC Scheme part of MTCTE. 
For implementation of ComSeC scheme NCCS has 3 divisions i.e., Security Assurance Standards (SAS), Security Lab Recognition (SLR) and Security Certification (SC). For more details, visit the NCCS website www.nccs.gov.in. NCCS is entrusted with the task of establishment of Centre of Excellence in Telecom Security Domain. NCCS is also involved in supporting activities for evaluation of hardware and the integrity of the supply chain of Telecom Network Equipment.

Scheme: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme
Question: Does Research Associate comes under category of job a NCCS?
Answer: Research Associateship is neither a job nor an assurance of a job with the NCCS. Selected candidate has to enter into a contract with NCCS.

Scheme: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme
Question: Is the contract period extendable?
Answer: Yes, it is extendable by one year, on the recommendations of Performance Appraisal Committee.

Scheme: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme
Question: What are the other terms and conditions of the scheme?
Answer: Refer to the latest RA notification published on the NCCS website for more details regarding general conditions of the contract.

Answer: Refer to the Annexure II of RA notification published on NCCS website.
